messages.text: You are forced to stop and observe what is going on around you, it's an awesome sight.  The once blue sky is turning a greenish black off to the west.  Seemingly miles away to begin with, the turmoil quickly engulfs you.

You are forced to stop and observe what is going on around you, it's an awesome sight.  The once blue sky is turning a greenish black off to the west.  Seemingly miles away to begin with, the turmoil quickly engulfs you.
Would you like to leave?
Under the rushing water you spot a rusty old hatch.  Would you like to open it?
The old road has many travelers.  Some of them approach you in a friendly manner, hands outstretched and palms open.  Will you stop and talk?
The humans who approach are in poor shape indeed.  Tattered clothing and hollow faces underline their plight.  Will you donate some food and water to these hopeless souls?
After your generous donation the perked up family gathers together their belongings and heads down the road west,  to Turnstil.
When you reach down to donate food to these "hopeless" souls, they twist and transform into ghoulish forms.  Under the spell of an unknown witch, the undead attack you while your guard is down.
Hideous cackles dance through your head as you trod down the old road.  Are they real or just a figment of your imagination?
The looming trees crack and twist as they notice your presence and attack!
The Turnstil militia barracks.  All the baracks are build from the same mold. One building stands out due to its larger size.
The main gate to the village of Turnstil.
The Turnstil Militia's training ground.  There are many land types to train on here  including swamp, forest, river, mountain, and open land.  A most remarkable layout.

You notice the townspeople meandering toward the grand building in the center of this square.  Beautiful oaks fill the square, complemented by ashen bushes.  A rotund man dressed in billowing yellow and red robes, flanked by two horn blowers......

....steps onto a big crate and unrolls a parchment.  The golden tassels ruffle in the wind as he bellows for all to hear, "Hear ye, Hear ye. Good people of Turnstil.  By Decree of the Overlord of Allstin, the great and wise Lamsor Orlansor has...

...ordered the manhunt for the despicable enemy of the people named Jurol Knarl.  This man is rightfully accused of murdering the lovely Queen Thantro of the House of Allstin.  He was seen fleeing the scene of the disgusting murder.  All ye of..

...bravery and skill who deem yourselves supporters of the House of Allstin and the great Town of Turnstil, are hereby invited to join in the manhunt for this vile consort of mayhem.  To join the fray, report to the captain of the barracks in the...

...southeast part of town within 5 days.  And as always, let us pray for the House of Allstin that they may lead us true and right as Thoron has ordained them do."  To a blare of horns, the man rolls up his parchment and goes on his way.

The Captain of the militia stands and greets you as you enter the building.  He is a man of wide girth, tanned skin and flowing brown hair.  He wears the crest of Allstin upon his plated chest.  At his side, his weapon of choice, the broadsword.
He clears his throat, "I am Alax, Captain of  the Turnstil militia.  Have you come to join in the hunt?"
Alax turns and walks away.  "Then we have no further business together.  Good day."  He sits behind his large cherry wood desk and shuffles through some papers.

"Excellent.  You have much to do.  You must prove your battle readiness to us in the training ground.  You will be matched against Allstin's finest, the Blood Dogs.  They are an elite group of fighters and assasins who test the mettle...

...of mercenaries like yourself.  You didn't think we take just anyone?!  Hah!  To hunt down Jurol we need not bring fodder.  We need men of courage and honor and loyalty.  Go now to the training ground east of here and meet the challengers."

Two enormous men decked in full plate guard the training ground entrance.  One speaks, "The training ground is only open to men of honor who serve the land of Allstin and the Town of Turnstil.  Be off with you."  They slam the door.

Two enormous guards greet you at the gate.  "Search the training ground and face the challenge.  You will meet the Blood Dogs.  They are already prepared for you and are waiting somewhere in the training area.  Be prepared.  Good luck."
The guards shake their heads in disgust.  "That was mettle?  Honor?  Courage?  You were screaming like little girls!  Come back later when you learn how to fight."
"Well done, well done.  You have proven yourselves worthy.  Meet the rest of the group soon near the east gate to the Castle Glisoor.  Do not delay, for time is of the essence."
Two of the Captains men ride up to you.  "You are keeping this manhunt from getting under way.  We have already lost precious time.  You were told to meet us.  Now, you will come with us, please?"
Your searching reveals an ambush in the waiting which you have just foiled!  The odds are in your favor as you hear the guards behind you yell their praise!  The battle is joined.
Having defeated the Blood Dogs you have proven yourself worthy.  The clerics of Turnstil arrive and take care of the wounded on the spot.
You are not prepared!  A hail of crossbow bolts engulf you as you are caught in the middle of an ambush, compliments of the Blood Dogs!  Maybe if you had been searching for them....

After a long, tedious journey through the Waywest Mountains, you hope to find some much needed food and sleep in the village of Turnstil. Some time ago, your old friend Thyrr wrote that he was retiring to that peaceful little town...
A large steel door sits ajar and the friendly guards let you pass.
A stand of large oak and pine trees.  Each tree is a full ten feet across and seventy feet tall.  Most impressive.
Someone has dropped a sack here.  Most likely from some long forgotten training session as the bag is quite worn.  The sack is partially buried in the surrounding dirt.  Would you like to uncover it?
The sack contains a few coins and a map.
The old sign reads, "Brunar, East.  Turnstil, North."
The sign reads, "Welcome to the town of Turnstil.  All hail the house of Allstin. May good fortune befall all those who enter.  Be warned - crime does not pay in our fair city."

The Staff of Seeking suddenly begins to quiver and hum.  It turns bright blue.  A blinding flash of light streaks out of the end of the staff and blows a hole 3 feet wide in front of you.  Care to investigate?
Inside the hole is an unremarkable piece of a spear.  As you look closer you can see the markings of Berhune.  You have found a piece of the Spear of Light!
The official colors of Turnstil.
The Turnstil Graveyard.  Many of the towns finest are buried in this pristine, well groomed resting spot.
"Tocharde Brungro - Mayor, 453-509 BG"
Winds pick up, your eyes grow blurry.  You black out momentarily.  You can feel more than see the vast sea pass beneath you.
You shake the cobwebs out of your head and realize you have been teleported to an unknown island in the middle of a vast sea.
Up in the air you sail, flying over a vast sea.  As the effect of flying wears off, you set down on a mysterious island in the middle of this vast sea.
Nothing happens.
A boat of solid construction.  You can either set out to sea or sail back to the mainland with this trusty craft.
A concealed shelf reveals some fishing equipment.  Do you want to take it?
An empty shelf.
"No fishing allowed."
The coast ahead is far too rocky, you must turn back.
A sign hanging on the door proclaims, "Everstay Inn.  Best price in all the land of Allstin."  Would you like to enter?

The inside of this cozy restaurant seems bigger than the outside.  Large round oaken tables adorned with local flora fill the main room.  The waitress greets you and seats you at a huge oak table.  It is very busy.  A popular place.
You notice a smaller room in the back of the restaurant, as well as a kitchen area and a stairway.  You get up from your table and begin exploring.

The waitress comes over to take your order.  "All meals come with water and fresh bread and are served home style with enough for everyone."  The aroma in the restaurant backs her statement.  "What will you have?"
The fish is excellent.  Very fresh and tasty. Well worth the price.
The pasta is a little underdone, but the sauce is rich and zesty.  A good value.
The chicken falls off the bones.  Excellent choice!
The chili is hot and spicy, with more beef than beans.  An excellent value.
After picking over the scraps, it's time to pay the check.  The waitress comes over.  "Who will be paying?"
"Thank you very much for dining with us.  I hope you enjoyed your meals!"  You leave with a full belly.
The name fits the brew.  A hearty round of Jimmie's wicked ale will end your night rather quickly.  This stuff packs a punch.
Weak and bland.  More musty than raspberry/apple.
The real stuff.  Excellent honey flavor.
A fine choice.  A hearty red.  Great full  body flavor and no heavy tannin taste.
After downing the swill, it's time to belly up to the barkeep.  A husky man grunts, "Who's payin for the stuff?"
The bar is overrun with the local folks.  A sweating, husky man is sloshing swill to them.  He is wearing more swill than he is serving.  "What will ya have?"
A small businessman hawks his wares.
A woman is sitting out on her front porch crying.  Do you approach?

She speaks, "You are so kind to be concerned about me.  We need more people in this town like you.  My brother lives in the town of Brunar;  a town not as safe as Turnstil.  His land has been raided by thieves and he has lost everything....

...that was dear to him.  I received a letter from him asking for my help.  I am but one woman.  I would like to go there and help him, but I have children and responsibility here.  I cannot go.  I want to send him this package containing.....

...what savings I have and some gems passed down through our family, but I cannot find anyone honest enough who is willing to brave the lands beyond Turnstil and deliver it."  Her face brightens a bit.  "Will you help me?"
"Thank you.  Thank you very much.  Here is the package and a map to his house.  Please hurry.  He is counting on me."  The woman hands you the map and package and goes inside.
A woman sits on her porch crying.  She sees you and runs back in the house and slams the door.
A depressed young man is leaning against the side of his home.  Do you approach?
He greets you suspiciously.  You explain to him who you are and why you are there.

"You don't have it!  My sister sends the likes of you to help me!  What a mistake.  I should not have asked for her help.  No, she should have asked for help from honorable people.  Get off my land."  He goes inside and closes the shutters.
As you pass the man yells profanities at you.  A few locals give you odd looks.  This is not helping your reputation.
The man thanks you profusely.  "I haven't much left, but I do have these."  He hands you a pair of oars.  "They are for my boat.  You can have it.  Thank you."
"I understand.  I guess I will have to find a different way."  She sobs her way into the house and closes the door.
You are greeted warmly by the waitress.  "Back so soon!  Go ahead, have a seat."  She scurries off.
A young man waves at you from his window.  "Everything is going great now, thanks!  Oh, yeah.  I forgot to tell you where the boat is.  Here is a map to it!"
A young man yells to you -
"Great seeing you again!"
"Thank you for all of your help!"
"You people are great.  Thanks again!"
"My sister and I thank you again!"
"Be safe out there.  Thanks again!"
You find, while searching, a secret door buried under some loose earth.  What a discovery!  Will you enter?
A long, narrow, musty passage leads you under the sea itself.  Who knows why it was built.  It is very ancient indeed.  You emerge on an island in the middle of this sea.
Under some sand you discover a trap door.  Will you enter?
After a long journey under the sea itself you arrive back on the mainland.
"Keep up the good work.  He needs those items.  Please hurry!"  She sends you on.

"You did it!  My brother and I thank you.  As a token of my appreciation, I want to give you something my mother gave me when I was a child.  She told me it was for good luck.  Your help is proof that it works.  Here, take it."
A woman sticks her head out the window and shouts -
Smoke billows from the chimney.  A sign proclaims, "Finest Armor In The Land Of Allstin."  Suits of armor hang in the open entrance.  You may shop at your leisure.
Hidden in the woods you discover a small group of huts.  Will you investigate?
A small hut houses an elven woman with three children.  They are busy playing together.
A clean, well kept hut houses an elven man feeding his newborn son.
A small but well kempt home.
A small hut lies against the forest backdrop.  A sign reads, "Goods For Sale."  Do you enter?

A small but well kempt hut.  A slender elf emerges from his home.  He speaks, "You have stumbled upon our homes and discovered our secret village.  I would ask that you leave us alone and allow us to maintain our seclusion.  We are a ...
An empty hut.
A small but well kept hut is empty of all activity.
This door is open, but you sense a powerful magic aura surrounding the frame.
An elderly woman sees you passing.  She yells out to you, "Hello!  Strangers such as yourselves need nourishment.  Care for a cup of tea and a few biscuits?"

"Come in, come in."  You enter a small house with all of the touches of home.  Small clay statuettes line the shelves of a gorgeous display cabinet.  Fine glassware fills the rest of the space.  This lady is loaded.  You are served tea and biscuits.

"My name is Treena.  I came long ago to this land from across the great sea.  Treacherous journey it was.  I wouldn't want to travel on that sea without a stout set of oars in my hands."  You notice her hands must have done some rowing........
....as they are rough and calloused.  Treena asks, "Do you want to take some food with you?"
"Here you are.  Thank you for your company.  You come back any time!"  Treena fills your sack with food and you say your farewells.
Treena sticks her head out the window.  "Come in, come in.  Refill your supplies.  You are no longer strangers, you are friends.  Friends help each other whenever they are able."
Treena runs outside to greet you.  "Hi again.  Nice to see you.  I have plenty of extra mutton from dinner yesterday.  You really should take some, as it will spoil soon."
Treena meets you on the road.  "Hi again, friends.  I have some extra bread I just baked for myself and I seem to have made too much.  You should take some.  It's fresh out of the oven!"
"Do you take Treena up on her offer?"
Quest 2, North west sector.
Quest 3, South central sector
Quest 4, central east sector.
A huge cheer erupts as the hunting party leaves castle Glisoor in search of Jurol Knarl.  You are too late.
The gates of this tiny village are locked up tight.  A smallish human man in his mid 40's walks up to the gate.  "C'mon in!"  He opens the gate.
A strange old man wanders out of his house.  "Cost ya 10 gold ta git past this bridge.  It's a toll bridge, ya know."  Do you pay the old man?
The man turns and mutters, "Always the same.  Durn fools never want to part with their money.  Ohhhh BORIS!  Time to collect!"  An immense, grotesque beast emerges from the house and comes after you.
Who will pay?
The old man smiles, "Hey Boris, looks like I get to eat good tonight for once!"  He lets you pass.
The sign reads, "Turnstil - North."
A dark, damp cave opens before you.  A recently extinguished fire still smoulders.
A dark, damp cave leads back into the mountains.
The inhabitants of the caves are here, hovering together in the darkness.  You can barely make out four human shapes.  Would you like to approach them?

A family of four shabbily dressed humans are here.  A mother, father and two small girls.  The father speaks, "Why do you persecute us?  It isn't enough to be cast from our city in shame, but you still must hunt us like animals!  Why?"
He grabs a nearby rock and hurls it in your direction.  Do you attack him back?

The father falls down and begins sobbing.  His wife runs to comfort him.  She yells, "You have done enough, leave us alone.  We have nothing left for you to steal.  Go back to your precious city and leave us to live in peace."

You defeat the once proud but now broken father easily.  His wife runs to him as he lay dying, "Jor, you have always been a good man.  Rest peacefully now, my love."  The woman then looks up at you, "I swear by my husbands death I will have my...

...revenge on you.  How dare you slaughter a helpless man.  What kind of people are you?"  She stares at you with pure hatred burning in her eyes, gathers her two young children, and runs out of the cave into the wilderness.
The two huddle together hoping you will leave them in peace.  The two children stand back against the far wall, fear paralyzing them.  Do you offer them help?
The family gathers together and watches you leave them in peace.

The woman speaks, "No one can help us.  We have been accused of stealing and destroying the Icon of Ahcrahn.  We didn't do it.  The evidence was against us and we were cast out of the city.  Only proof of our innocence will return us to our home."

She continues, "The Icon of Ahcrahn brought good fortune to our city.  When it was stolen, all of our crops failed, children became ill, happy neighbors fought and stole from each other."  Her face brightens, "If you could find the icon...

...our names would be cleared and our city would be restored.  We do not have much, but our city would repay you greatly.  Could you, would you help us?  Will you find the Icon of Ahcrahn, restore our good name, and save our city?"
"Wonderful!  She leaps from her husbands side and hugs you warmly.  When you find it, and I know you will, bring it back here and together we will go back to Ahcrahn.  Thank you.  You are kind."

The woman stands up proudly, "I understand.  Do not concern yourself with our problems.  On the other hand, if you change your mind we'll be here."  With that the family returns to the darkness of the cave.  You leave.
The family wishes you luck in finding the Icon of Ahcrahn and sends you on your way.

Tears flow from all in the family as you present them the Icon of Ahcrahn.  The father approaches, "Thank you, let us now return triumphantly to our city and restore it to prosperity."  Do you go with them to the city?"
The mother speaks, "But you will not get a reward.  I'm sure we will be able to clear our names now, but you will get nothing.  Please, come with us and accept a reward."

The father speaks, "You truly are a humble, noble lot.  I had my doubts about you but you have proven yourself to me.  Here take this, it is only for the power of good that it is to be used, and you have shown me that.  My thanks."
A huge, grey cloud hangs over this town.  The hinges of the iron gate are rusted and hanging open.  You easily push down the gate.

As you look over the town, you shake your head.  What has happened here?  All of the other towns are green and plush.  This town is brown and dying.  No crops grow.  Trees are dead or dying.  Crows pick over the remains of dead cattle.  Strange.
The east gate of Ahcrahn.
An old and decrepit farm house.  Would you like to explore it?

The farmhouse is in obvious disrepair.  An old man sits hunched over at the only intact piece of furniture in the home.  His head rests in his hands and he doesn't seem to notice you.  What would you like to do?
The man does not move.  Now what?
When you shake the man he is very dead.  His stiff body is hard to move as rigor mortis has set in.  He is leaning over a letter.  Would you like to read it?
Respecting the mans privacy, you elect not to read the letter.  Now what would you like to do?
You notice the man is leaning over a letter.  Would you like to read it?

Jess,  The Icon is gone.  We have convicted the Lurha family of the crime and have sentenced them to permanent exile from our city.  But times grow worse.  Crops die.  People become ill for no reason.  I have become ill as well.  I do not think....

...I will last myself.  Nothing will grow so our people starve.  The constable himself has no idea what we can do.  Only the Lurha family knows where the Icon is.  They refuse to tell us and have condemned us all to death.  If only we...

...had the Icon back.  I fear it is too late.  I have already buried your mother, Tess.  I miss her so.  I write this to you, my dear daughter, as my last breath escapes me.  Take care of yourself and your children.  I will miss them.  Love,  Peotre."
You notice the man is dead.
The headstone reads, "My beloved Tess.  Loved by many, missed by all."
The father bows his head and utters some words.....

....you appear in a most run down town.  As soon as you appear the town constable staggers out of his house.  He yells, "There they are....they have stolen the Icon of Ahcrahn!  Guards, sieze them!  Seize them all!"  Some guards stumble out of.....
...a nearby barracks and move to seize you.  What will you do?
A few weakened warriors will give it their best effort.

You have defeated the last of the Ahcrahn militia.  The constable approaches you, "You have beaten the last of our people.  I am the only one left.  A constable has no place without his people."  With that he plunges his own dagger deep into his...

...chest and drops dead at your feet.  The father of the family speaks, "I thank you for bringing the Icon to us.  I regret to say I cannot respect you for what you have done.  Leave this place.  We alone will attempt to rebuild our city.  Do not....
...return here, for you are no longer welcome.  Your evil sickens us."  The father speaks some words and you are transported out of the town.
The town beyond the gate is dark and gloomy.  Touching the gate repels you backward with a jolt.
The guards are in no mood for discussion.  You are easily taken with your guard down and escorted to the town dungeon.
The doors to the dungeon are locked up tight.  What would you like to try?
Nice effort, no success.  Now what?
No luck.  Nothing happens.  What would you like to try?
Doesn't work.  Now what?
Nothing interesting happens.  What now?
Success!  The lock pops open.
The spell allows you to easily slip through the cracks around the door and unlock it from the other side.
Your brute strength smashes open the door.
Stairs lead up to a door.  Would you like to ascend them?
The door opens to the outside where, surprisingly, it is unguarded.  Seems you were to be forgotten about.
Your effort reveals a crack outlined like a door in the very rock.  Do you open it?
Behind the door is a passage through the rocks.
The door to the training grounds is locked tight.  Two burly guards stand at it and tell you to get lost until you talk to the captain.
The guards take your pass and let you in to the training grounds.
Alax meets you at the door.  "Have you had a change of heart?"
"Take this.  The guards will take it from you and allow you to enter the training ground."  He hands you a writ of entrance to the training area.

Alax greets you at the door.  He looks displeased.  "You need to go through the training grounds.  It is directly to the east.  I would give you a map but it's only 100 yards away!"  He mutters and shuts the door.

Alax greets you with a huge smile.  "You have proven your worth to me and to the village of Turnstil in the land of Allstin.  Meet commander Tregel at the east gate of Castle Glisoor.  They leave in five days.  Do not be late.  Good luck to you."
Alax is busy chewing out some would be heroes about crying like little girls.  It is best not to disturb him.

Alax is busy signing up some new recruits.  He looks over at you and mentions to the group, " You pathetics will have a hard time matching up to the standards set by them!"  He points to you and shoves the newbies off to the training ground.
Alax is not here.  The place is empty.
The men escort you to the meeting place.
The east gate of Castle Glisoor.  A lone guard paces back and forth in front of the gate, his concentration remarkable.  He notices you milling around and tells you to move along.
The south gate of castle Glisoor.  The gate is unattended.
What would you like to do?

All the pounding and commotion has brought the attention of the local guards.  About a dozen show up and quite firmly ask you to leave.  They inform you to make an appointment at the town hall.  Will you leave?
A wise choice.  The guards give you a map to the town hall and send you on your way.

The captain speaks, "We are a just and fair town.  We will tell you again.  Leave this place and make an appointment at the town hall.  If you do not leave, we will be forced to take action against you."  Will you leave?

All the commotion has summoned the town guards.  They are quick to notice it is you who was pounding on the door the first time.  They are not as kind this time.  You are issued a citation for Disorderly Conduct.

The captain speaks, "You are hereby ordered to appear in person within the next five days at the Justice of the Peace to face trial or pay the fine.  The fine is 500 gold.  Do not fail to show up."  They ride off.
As you set foot through the gate, two castle guards appear.  They ask what business you have coming through the gate.  You show them the letter and are escorted to the castle.

They are not as kind this time.  You are issued a citation for disorderly conduct.  The captain speaks, "You are hereby ordered to appear in person within the next five days at the Justice of the Peace to face trial or pay the fine.  The fine.....
.....is 500 gold.  Do not be late.  Good day."  They ride off.
The lock pops open.  You easily slide open the gate and slip inside the castle walls.
With a tremendous effort, the gate gives way.  You may now slip inside the castles outer walls.
The south gate of Castle Glisoor.  Three guards pace back and forth in front of the gate, their concentration remarkable.  One notices you milling around and tells you to move along.
The town courthouse.  The Justice of the Peace sits behind a large desk.  Two of his aides are seated one on each side.
The town hall.  The desk clerk asks what you need.
The clerk sighs, "I'm sorry, the King is currently booked up.  You will have to check later."

"Ah, yes.  I do have an opening for you to meet with the King.  Let me just sign you in.  Now, you all sign here.  Now here.  Here.  And finally, here."  After jumping through the required hoops, you get your appointment with King Allstin.

The clerk continues, "Here is the required paperwork you will need to present to the guards in order to have your meeting with King Allstin.  I hope you have something to talk about as the king is a busy man."  She hands you some papers.
"Thank you for visiting.  Come back soon."

The guards usher you to the criminal waiting area.  One of them speaks to you.  "You have been charged with Disorderly Conduct.  You may plead guilty, pay the fine and have your names cleared.  You may plead not guilty and face trial.  Or, ...

...you may plead no contest and throw yourselves on the mercy of this court.  Your names will be called shortly and you will be brought before Justice Swyfft."  It looks like you will have some time on your hands.  This adventure is not going well.
What would you like to do while you are waiting amongst the lower forms of the inhabitants of Turnstil, of which you are now members....momentarily?
Don't you ever learn?  Trying to break out of the holding pen proves fruitless.  There are far too many guards and no way to avoid them.  You are immediately brought before Justice Swyfft.

He speaks, "So, these are the ruffians who were trying to break into the castle?  And now they have tried to escape!  No matter what your plea, you are found guilty of disorderly conduct and attempting to escape justice.  Your penalty...500 gold....
...for Disorderly Conduct and 5,000 gold for trying to escape.  A total of 5,500 gold.  You will pay now or be put in prison.  Who will pay?
Justice Swyfft speaks.  "Let this be a lesson to you.  Justice is swift in Turnstil.  Criminals and ruffians beware.  I will not tolerate this type of activity in my town!"  You are escorted out.

Justice Swyfft turns beet red.  "You don't have enough to pay the fine?  Well, you are going to have to spend some time in our cozy little prison.  Sentence - 45 days.  And of course, you will donate your items to charity as you have no use for them....
....while sitting in jail."  The guards quickly grab you and remove your belongings.  You are thrown into the town dungeon to rot for 45 days."
A Turnstil captain and sergeant are working some troops.  They spot your escape attempt and attack.
A Turnstil lieutenant and sergeant are being escorted by two guards.  They spot you and attack.
A patrol of four Turnstil guards spots you and attacks.
The cell door is locked and a heavy iron bar is braced across it from the other side.  A most formidable prison cell.
Quite an effort.  You are an accomplished opener of locks!  It pops open and you make good your escape.
Your tremendous strength explodes the door.  Nothing remains but splinters and twisted iron.  You make good your escape.
Risky, but it works.  From the outside of the door you easily dismantle the barring mechanism and turn the huge lock counter-clockwise to free your friends.  You make good your escape.
A contingent of guards was working on their marching until they spotted you round the corner.  They attack!
You are sitting in a cell.  What would you like to try?
Torches fail to illuminate the area very brightly.  There is a severe lack of light in this dungeon!
The cell door hangs open.
The castle guard notices you and sounds the alarm before they attack.  Sneaking onto the castle grounds was probably not a good idea.
The sign reads, "Wizard's Hide-A-Way".

A husky old dwarf lumbers over and holds out his hand like a stop sign.  "This here is a toll bridge.  500 gold to cross.  This is the only way across this river, and since I'm the only one who can drop the barrier, I suggest you pay, or ya don't cross."
Ouch.  You run headlong into an invisible barrier of some sort.  From a nearby shack a figure emerges.
Will you pay?
"Fine.  Have fun on that half of the river!"  He lumbers over to his shack and slams the door.  A tremendous jolt pushes you back from the barrier.
The dwarf thanks you and lowers the barrier.  He yells as you ride off, "Remember, this is a one way pass.  You will have to pay for each crossing!"
The invisible barrier is in front of you.  What would you like to try?
The barrier is no longer present.  You may cross the bridge.
You circumvent the barrier and can continue on your way.
Whoa!  Better duck, 'cause that lightning bolt is coming right back at ya off the barrier!  Too late.  You get sizzled.
The flow of water here is churning and not crossable.  You must turn back.  You scamper up to dry land; happy to be in one piece, and not in the churning waters.
A tiny shack lies in front of a bridge.  But when you approach, it disappears and moves to the other side of the bridge!
You sail through the air avoiding the magic traps set by the dwarf.  You set down on his front door step.  He is quite startled.
The pulse of magic courses through your veins.  Your head spins as the world goes black.  Only the caster maintains a keen sense of awareness as the magic flows through the air.
You shake your head as the world reappears with a gradual brightening.  You realize you have teleported right to the front door of the shack.  The dwarf is quite surprised.
You lift aloft, floating above the ground beneath you.  With butterflies in your stomach, you gently set down right on the front door step of the shack.  The dwarf is quite surprised to see you.
The invisible barrier is gone.  What would you like to try?
A rickety old furfoot walks up to you.  "Sooo..you've solved my riddle.  Here is your reward."  He hands you a magical staff.   The old shack and the rickety old furfoot then disappear.
Your wizard's eye sees an invisible barrier just a few paces ahead of you. It is located in front of the bridge and extends over it 10 yards.  You would have run smack into it.

Your searching reveals an invisible barrier just a few yards in front of you. It is located just this side of the bridge, and extends over the bridge 10 yards past it.   Lucky you saw it or you would have smacked into it.

You sit and wait patiently while other cases are being heard.  One man pleads guilty to theft of a mule and is sentenced to 20 days in jail.  A woman pleads not guilty to bribery and gets a court date.  Finally, after a lengthy delay, your.....
....names are called.  Justice Swyfft reads aloud.  "Docket number 113244A-17B.  Charge:  Disorderly conduct.  How do you plead?"
You enter your guilty plea and face the fine.  Justice Swyfft speaks, "The fine is 500 gold.  Who will pay?
The gate is currently unguarded, but your presence soon raises attention and two guards show up.
The larger guard speaks, "Ahh, you have an appointment.  Please, come with us.  King Allstin awaits.  Enjoy your visit within Castle Glisoor."  They escort you to the castle.

The sickly green turns darker and darker until a viridescent black is all you can see.  Streaks of lightning crackle through the blackness.  Suddenly the sky opens up and fiery balls of molten earth plumett towards you at tremendous speed.

Small fires erupt wherever a ball of fire strikes.  Then, as quickly as the fiery rain began, it stops.  All is quiet except for an occasional crackle of lightning above.  All is too quiet.  No sound.  None.  The daily sounds of chirping birds....
...and barking dogs are gone.  The sky remains an eerie green-black.  The clouds boil and churn above you, turning over and into themselves like dough being kneaded.
A rickety old wagon rides up to you.  A jolly, stout dwarf jumps down and says, "Have I got some deals fer ya!"  He opens his wagon and shows you what he has to offer.
A sign hangs in front of the building, "The Herring Bone Inn."  Will you enter?
The lake is very shallow here.  It is about 20' deep.  The sandy bottom is reached easily while you hold your breath.  You begin searching the bottom of the lake.
Who will attempt this?

Suddenly a sharp pain shoots up your arm. Someone has set a trap in this lake to catch something very big.  It has ended up catching you.  A bear-trap like vice has clamped down on your arm doing considerable damage.
Next time you will think twice about jumping into a lake.  Your party manages to pull your limp body from the water.
The waters part and you can walk down onto the bottom freely.  To the left and right, confused fish swim up to and away from the edge of the water curtain that has cut their world in half.

While walking on the sandy floor, you notice the teeth of a bear-like trap protruding through the sand.  You can easily avoid stepping on it and do.  You wonder what type of creature was meant to be caught in a lake by a trap like that?
A hideous creature juts its head through the wall of water to your right.  It sees you, leaps out of the water and, baring its teeth, attacks.
You send the beast to a watery grave.  You can continue your search of the lake floor.

Your searching uncovers a cleverly hidden secret door disguised as a mossy patch of rock.  You remove the stones and discover a small sealed door with a ring in the center.  Would you like to open it?

With a great sigh, a balloon of stale, very damp air rushes past you blowing your hair away from your faces.  A deep staircase descends almost straight down into the darkness.  Would you like to descend?
You detect a very strong magic aura around the door.  What would you like to try?
Your spell fizzles.  The magically sealed door stays closed.
The area around the door pulses and glows a bright whitish-yellow.  The pulsing slows as does the glowing until the area around the door is still.  The magic aura around is dispelled.
The magic aura jolts you with electricity.  It does not enjoy being kicked.
The beautiful Lake Miwson.  You think you catch sight of some sort of fish disturb the surface of the water and then vanish.
The locked door is at your feet.  What would you like to try?
When you touch the magic door, it discharges electricity of great intensity which engulfs your entire party.

You close the heavy door behind you.  The stairs wind deep into the earth.  You find yourself ankle deep in water and sludge from the high level of seepage here.  The stairs end in a hallway running away from you to the north.
The door is magically locked and sealed.  Nothing but you can get in or out.... hopefully.

You drive the spikes like wedges around the door.  Nice job.  Maybe you should consider driving tent stakes for the circus!  With the spikes in place, nothing except you will be able to get in or out of here.
You discover the reason the seal was on the door.  A roaring thunder fills your ears as Lake Miwson empties into the long lost dungeon.

The roaring cascade of water barrels down the hallway headlong into you.  You are not sure whether it was the bashing against the stone walls and floor or simply drowning which ended your days.  You are sure that you are dead.
Although you are able to breath due to your water breathing, you are bounced around like a bobber in a hurricane.  Ouch!
The roaring water shoots you out a flood relief opening and you are happy (and lucky) to be alive.
The closed door is in front of you.  What would you like to do?
You hear through the door a lot of thrashing and gurgling.  Sounds like parting water.
After a long climb you reach the top of the stairs.  The dungeon door is above your head.  Would you like to open it?
The waters churn and boil behind their magical curtain.
The sign reads, "Turnstil - Old Road West.  Brunar - East."

You surprise an old dwarf.  He jumps up screaming, "Hey!  Get outta my house.  I got plenty-a gold here and don't like you young 'uns tryin' ta ruff me up fer it.  Git outta here or y'all be sorry!"  Do you leave?
The old dwarf scratches his head, "Oh Boris one through nine, we got work to do."  Nine immense beasts burst through the back door and attack, along with the dwarf.
A search of his house provides you with the treasure to which the dwarf was referring.
The outer gates of Turnstil.
A Temple of Berhune.  A cleric greets you, "Welcome my brothers.  How may the good God Berhune help your suffering?"
A glowing citadel stands before you.  A voice booms out, "Enter ye of faith and receive salvation."  Will you enter?
A rickety staircase leads to the surface.  Would you like to exit the dungeon?
Under the burning bush you discover a trap door leading down.  Would you like to descend?
A creaky wooden staircase descends some ten feet and puts you in front of a door.
The strong magic aura continues to wipe out the magic strength of your party.  Your spells momentarily falter due to the power of this magic.

An overwhelming sensation of magic surges through you as you approach.  Your compass spins wildly and goes dead.  The magic using abilities of your party are sapped as those members of the party feel extremely powerless.
Those with magic abilities stagger and stumble as their power is sucked from them.  Even those with no power left feel the drain on their bodies.

Your searching reveals a small, loose rock about 3' high on the southern wall.  Investigating further you see this rock is a keystone for a larger group of rocks higher up on the wall.  It is obvious from this configuration pulling the keystone...
...will cause this section of the wall to collapse, thus revealing whatever lies beyond.  You do not know, however, in which direction the rocks will fall.  Will you pull the keystone?

The keystone lets loose a good size chunk of wall which falls away from you revealing a dusty, very dark passage beyond.  It is obvious this passage has been untouched for much longer than the rest of this dungeon.

Your magic eye reveals a small loose rock about 3' high on the southern wall.  Investigating further you see this rock is a keystone for a larger group of rocks higher up on the wall.  It is obvious from this configuration pulling the keystone...
Where once stood a solid wall, only rubble remains.
That is a solid chunk of wall.  Ouch.
A most bizarre statue startles you.  A figure of a mummy, a full 7' high, made of solid silver.  His arms are outstretched as if trying to reach you.

A huge statue of a silver mummy can be found in each of the four corners of the room.  Larger than the others you have seen, these beasts stand a full 9' in height with their arms folded over their chests and heads bowed down.

A gruesome sight indeed.  A fate worse than death has befallen a previous group of adventurers.  Their weapons drawn and shields in front, they function not as the party is stone.  But wait, two of the party are not stone.  They yell at you...
....for aid.  You discover why they want your help.  Two medusa emerge from the darkness and resume their attack.  Will you help them?
Before one of the poor party members who was here before you was turned to stone, he dropped something very nice!
An ancient, wooden desk covered in years of dust sits across from you on the far wall.
The medusa make quick work of the two remaining adventurers and turn their attention to you!
You draw your weapons and make good the fight.
Although you have defeated the medusa, two brave men have given their lives.  You continue on, not knowing who these men were.  You only know they were brave and in need of help.

The surving fighter walks up to you.  "My comrades are dead.  My name is Maru.  I will join you in your quests if you will have me.  You show bravery and honor for joining the battle.  Will you accept me into your party?"
"I understand.  Thank you for my life.  I will repay you if we meet again."  Maru scoops up his belongings and heads off.

The lone survivor, a thief, approaches you.  "Thanks for your assistance.  I could have managed without you but, nonetheless, thanks.  I was thinkin'.  You could use a hand in battle, and since I have nothing better to do, I guess I could...
...join up with you if you want.  My name is Regar.  What do you say?"
"Hey, no problem.  I just thought you guys could use the help.  See ya around."  Regar moves on.

The two survivors run up to you after the battle.  The fighter speaks, "My name is Maru, and this is Regar, a thief.  We are impressed with your skills.  We would like to join with you in your quests if you would have us.  What say you?"

"We understand.  You have your battles and we have ours.  It is unfortunate we could not combine our struggles.  Thank you for our lives.  If we can repay you at a later date, if ever our paths cross, it will be done."  With that, they leave.
"Excellent.  You will find my skills usefull indeed."  Maru packs his gear and looks eager to adventure.
"Good.  You will need my help.  Lets go."  Regar packs up his gear and takes his place at the rear of the party.

Maru is pleased.  "We are honored to join you.  Our debt to you is best repaid in this way.  We will stay with you as long as we are able."  Maru and Regar gather their belongings and join your ranks.
An ancient wooden roll-top desk rests here.  You note the drawers are closed as is the top.

Your searching reveals a letter in one of the drawers.  It reads, "We have secured the complex and are making ready to abandon it.  The traps are functioning well as your magic proves powerfull.  I have enclosed a map to the control room in....
...case we ever return here.  Hopefully that will be sooner than later."  The letter is signed, "Your servant in Darkness,  Kelsen Drook, Commander, Eastern Stronghold."

When you pass through this door, whispy images tear out of the silver statues to the east.  They begin gliding toward you very slowly.  You could easily out run them.  The visages are no longer silver, but look greenish, almost transparent.
The mummies are walking toward you.  What will you do?

When you pass through this door, whispy images tear out of the silver statues to the north.  They begin gliding toward you very slowly.  You could easily out run them.  The visages are no longer silver, but they look greyish, almost transparent.

When you pass through this door, whispy images tear out of the silver statues to the south.  They begin gliding toward you very slowly.  You could easily out run them.  The visages are no longer silver, but they look greyish, almost transparent.

A patrol of four officers emerges from the guardhouse.  The highest ranking of them as shown by his gleaming gobs of insignia speaks, "No one is allowed entrance except through the northern gates.  Turn back at once."  Do you leave?
The commander frowns.  "If you do not leave now, you will be considered enemies of the Cheltin People and we will be forced to strike against you."  He looks determined.  Will you obey and leave?
The Commander calls for the rest of his troops.  They attack you as promised.
You have wiped out the south western Garrison.  It will not take long for word of this outrage to reach the King.
The stairs lead down.  Take them?
The stairs lead up.  Take them?
Back in the restaurant.  Would you like to return to your table?
The innkeeper sits behind a modest oaken table.  "Will you be spending the night with us?"
"Ah, good.  Cost is 10 gold.  Each room can sleep 10 comfortably.  Who will be paying?"
"Sorry.  You do not have enough gold to stay with us.  Please come back when you do.  Good night."
"Thank you.  Here is your key.  You are in the main suite.  Room 2.  Take the stairs and your room is located directly across from the stairway.  Enjoy your stay."
A small home to a young lady and her two children.  The two boys scurry into the house when their mother calls them for dinner.
A small home to a young lady and her two children.  The two boys run at each other with sticks as swords yelling, "Have at you!!!"
A small home to a young lady and her two children.  One boy kneels over the other as the downed child screams at him, "Ouch, you numbskull. I said aim for the dirt not my shirt."
A small border village lies against the Vrawdil mountains.  The door is unlocked and easily pushes open.
The town well.  It is clean cold water serves this village well.
A deep well full of crisp clear water decends deep into the earth.  A sturdy ladder lowers into the depths.

You grab as big a gulp of air as you can and descend the ladder.  Wow, this well is deep!  You realize as your lungs are about to burst you cannot make it to the bottom.  You manage to scramble out of the well and regain your breath.
Luckily you are able to breathe down here.  You descend a full 200' or more.  At the bottom of the well there is a crude iron gate.

The grate rips open, revealing a long corridor heading east.  It is full of water.  The change in water pressure tumbles you into the corridor.  You regain your balance and realize you have travelled 100' and are still slowly being pushed eastward.
As you slowly move eastward,  you notice, above your head, a grate in the ceiling similar to the one you opened to get in here.  Would you like to make a grab for it?
Unbelievable.  Your attempt to open the grate dislodged some of the older stones in the well.  They tumble down on you.

You pass the grate in the ceiling and get washed out into the Bryne River.  The fall is 30' from the cliff to the river below.  You once again breathe the fresh air and shake the water out of your gear.
This will not be easy.  Who will try it?
You got it!  You grab the grate and deftly open it, and pull yourself into a damp hallway.  A long piece of hemp lies next to the grate and you pull yourselves up into the hallway!  Well done.
High in the canopy above, you spot what the local townsfolk were talking about.  The Nirak attack you on sight.
After defeating the Nirak you discover a pile of droppings nearby.  Would you like to search them?
After rummaging through Nirak feces and what could be human bone fragments, you discover something round and shiny!
You discover a pile of droppings nearby.  Would you like to search them?

All of these buildings seem to indicate this small assembly of homes is abandoned.  Strange screeching can be heard in the background, as if birds are about.  But when you look skyward, nothing is there.
Out of the corner of your eye you think you catch the glimpse of a small boy peering around the corner of the building to the southwest of you.

You were right.  The small boy runs but you easily grab him by his scruff and bring him before the party.  He can be no more than seven years, but his hollow eyes and terrorized face hide his age.  He bellows, "Leave, leave at once.  You will...
...be killed like all the rest.  They sing. You listen. You die.  Just like that.  Songs of death.  Wait.  You look strong.  Come.  Come with me.  You will help?"  Will you go with the boy?

The boy runs off yelling, "Fine.  You not strong.  You cowards.  They will kill you.  You will hear.  Then you will die....."  His voice trails off and is replaced by a loud squak.  From the sky humanoid birds attack.
Hopefully there are no more of them.  The boy was right.  Those birds are deadly.
The boy takes you to the home just to the northeast of you.

You enter the home.  The boy pushes aside a large rug from the middle of the floor and stomps two times.  After a long pause a trap door slowly opens.  He invites you to come in.  As your eyes adjust to the darkness you see why he...

...asked for your help.  What remains of this village is here in a fifteen by fifteen room, covered in their own filth and living in squallor.  What appears to be a leader to them steps forward.  He speaks, "Naese is my name.  I apologize for our...

...appearance.  What you see here has happened so quickly we have had no chance to get help from Turnstil.  It all began but a week ago.  Out of nowhere these beasts attacked, carrying off our young and elderly first, then singing that..

...song of death.  We cannot fight them.  The song of death lulls us into complacency and they devour us.  We have no chance without help.  I was sending the boy to Turnstil when you came upon him.  Please help us.  We have been...

...able to determine these beasts live somewhere in the forest south of our town.  Please seek out their nesting ground and destroy them.  Will you do this for us?  I do not have much.  If you help us, what is mine is yours.  Please?"

"Thank you.  When you are succesfull you will find us here.  If you are not, we will not speak again, for we will be devoured.  I eagerly await your victorious return."  With that, you depart in search of these beasts.

Naese lowers his head.  "I understand.  These problems are ours alone.  We will do our best against them.  Thank you for escorting my boy here.  Good day."  You leave.  The birds were waiting outside for someone to exit.  That someone was you.
You enter and tap the trap door twice.  Naese opens up and asks you how it's going.  Hearing you have not yet found the nest he bids you good luck and sends you on your way.
Some birds were waiting on you.  They attack on sight.

You enter the home, slide the rug out of the way and knock twice on the trap door.  Naese opens the door leerily.  You tell him the good news and he leaps from the dreary cellar along with what remains of the small village.  "Thank you brave.....

...people for freeing us of these beasts.  You are indeed good people.  As I said before I do not have much, but as promised what is mine is now yours."  He walks over to the nearby fireplace and reaches up into its throat.  He pulls out....

...a soot covered scabbard.  With a gentle puff of air Naese blows the dust off the scabbard and hands it to you.  "This, my friends, has been good to me.  Now it will be good to you.  Again, my thanks."  You accept the gift.
Naese is here with his boy.  He waves happily at you as you pass by.  The boy is actually starting to act like a boy of seven years should.
Naese is in the yard playing catch with his boy.  A young lady walks by and gives Naese a wink and a smile.  Seems all is well.
Naese and his boy are out tending the new garden.  Naese looks up and nods respectfully in your direction, then gets right back to pulling weeds.  All is well.
A strange sign hangs above the entrance.  It reads, "Impossible Quests."  Would you like to take a look inside?

What a rag-tag collection of characters.  Orcs, goblins, hobgoblins, elves, dwarves.  Never before have you seen such an odd collection of species.  You suppose this is a bar, but it wouldn't look it.  Unclean and unattended, you wonder who owns...

...this forsaken hole and how a profit is turned?   You must have been thinking out loud.  A large troll-like woman gives you an answer. "I'm the owner of Impossible Quests.  500 g.p. and you each get a mug.  Who's payin'?"
The woman grunts, "Hrrmph.  No money.  Not allowed to stay.  Good day."  You are escorted out.

The woman gladly accepts your money and, as promised, gives you each a silver mug with a platinum handle.  The mug is decorated with an etching of a lone paladin beheading a blue dragon.  The woman speaks, "Table in the corner.  Enjoy your stay."

You usher yourselves to the table stuck in what seems to be the darkest corner of the bar.  You are still wondering where you get the grog.  As you get settled in and place your mugs on the table something odd happens.  Out of thin air...

...a pitcher appears over your mug and fills it with grog.  Now that is service.  The rest of the party's mugs are filled with whatever was on their minds to drink.  Ale, wine, mead all flow into the mugs of silver and platinum.  Odd indeed.  The...

...grog tastes just like you thought it would.  Whenever your mug becomes empty, whatever you desire to drink appears and refills your mug.  A large rectangular table is centered in the center of the large room.  Around it mill a few...
...goblins and humans trying to get the attention of the large gnoll seated there.  He is hiring on people for some jobs he needs done.  Care to investigate?
You sit back down after deciding you are not interested in what he might have to offer.  The troll-like lady wanders over, "You ready to leave?"
The owner thanks you for stopping in and reminds you whenever you have a spare 500 gold you are welcome back.

She says okay and lets you return to your drinking.  That discussion at the center table is getting interesting.  You overhear someone mention a Maw and how no one can defeat it.  Would you like to take a look?
A large hobgoblin is decked out in full plate mail, which looks much more ornate than functional.  He hands you a parchment which lists his jobs.  He barks in crude common, "Which one?"
"Destroy the Maw?  Brave you are - or foolish.  I supply you with map.  5000 gold reward.  Deal?  I warn you - humans no kill maw yet."
"Okay.  Deal.  Here is map.  Zrack Floj."  You guess that is Gnollish for either good luck or no chance.  With map in hand you head out.
"Smart choice.  You no live anyway."  The Gnoll takes back the parchment.  Would you like to return to the table or leave?
As you approach this large alcove you spot, ahead of you, what appears to be large gaping green jaws hovering four feet in the air.  They spot you and attack!
Congratulations!  You have succeeded where many other adventurers have failed.   Among the scattered bones you find treasure.
You arrive safely on the shore of the beautiful lake.
An elderly gentleman sits behind a finely crafted roll top desk.  He takes a long draw on his pipe and asks you to sit down.  Will you?

He asks, "So, you seek Griloch?  He is here, be sure of that.  Also be sure he knows you seek him.  Griloch has opened a rip from the Abyss.  His minions are even now harassing the local folk.  Legend tells us he would return, and he has.  And worse..

..he has summoned the power to traverse planes.  No longer is he a mere projection from the Abyss.  He is  here.  I cannot tell you where he is, but I can tell you that you must destroy him.  For if you do not, all that these people have come to know..

..will be gone.  Griloch will destroy all of the good in this land and replace it with his unending evil.  This is your mission."  The old man takes another draw from his pipe and stares pensively into the rising smoke.
A small house typical of the city of Turnstil.  Slatted wooden roof, cherry wood walls and small square windows.  Very cozy.

..to begin your adventure.  Griloch's Revenge is the sequel to Prelude to Pestilence scenario.  Although playing PTP is not a prerequisite to Griloch's Revenge you may find some of the items from Prelude to Pestilence helpful.

Thank you for supporting Realmz and Fantasoft.  If you enjoy this adventure, please register it by following the instructions contained herein.  The cost is $14.00.  Thanks again and enjoy Griloch's Revenge.  -Sean Sayrs, Author.
A guard house for the village of Turnstil.  Currently it is unoccupied.
The official flag of Turnstil.
The inner gates of Turnstil.  They are locked.  A small eyeslit opens and a guard speaks through it to ask what your business is in Turnstil.  What do you answer?

The guard grunts back, "Adventure?  If it is adventure you seek see the captain of the guard in the largest barracks just past the graveyard.  Big manhunt is about to start.  Come in."  He opens the door.
The guard responds, "Food and drink.  Come in, come in.  We have many fine restaurants and pubs.  Enjoy your stay."  He opens the door.
The guard answers you, "A job?  You should go and see the town clerk.  There are always jobs available."  He opens the door.
The guard chuckles.  "Lost?  Well, you found your way this far.  Come in and see the map maker.  He'll set ya straight."  He opens the door.
The inner gates of Turnstil.
A few guards decked out in fine plate mail mill about.  They acknowledge you and continue about their duties.
A lone guard is here playing cards.  He looks up at you and asks if everything is okay.  Before you can respond he says, "Excellent.  Glad to hear that.  Have a great day.  Stay safe."
Two guards are here talking loudly.  You overhear one say that Griloch is nothing more than an old myth.  The other just shakes his head.
Three guards are here talking quietly amongst themselves.  You overhear them discuss a secret elvish community located somewhere far to the east of Turnstil.
You do not have a key for this room.  It is locked.
Your key slips easily into the door and you enter your room.

A closet.  An old man is sitting here.  He speaks.  "You may keep things here by clicking on the "shop" button and selling them to the closet.  To retrieve them, simply buy them back. There is a 10% restocking fee to retrieve your items."
Would you like to lock the door behind you after you leave?
You securely lock your suite door behind you.
Your room has been broken into!  The ruffians who perpetrated this act are still here.  They attack you on sight.  Luckily you caught them before they found the closet.
A quick search of the bodies reveals a little treasure.
A small sign hanging in the window proclaims this "Myriams Magic."
A long abandoned house.  No sign of occupants.  Boarded up and silent, no one has been here for countless years.

A low rumble fills your ears as an apparition of Thyrr appears.  He speaks, "Friends, I have grievous news.  Griloch has returned and begins anew his evil plan.  Further, he seeks revenge on those who previously defeated him in battle.....

...Those who were caught unaware are trapped in eternal spheres of agony.  Others were killed in a futile attempt to storm his castle.  I too was killed in that battle but, by evil means, Griloch has trapped my soul between planes.  Thus...
You teleport into the long abandoned house.  There are several rooms which you may explore.
You knock on the boards and they break, landing inside the house and banging loudly on the wooden floor.  Since you have made a door for yourselves would you like to look around?
You stand before a long abandoned, boarded up house.

A solitary round, maplewood table stands in the corner.  One chair sits neatly pushed into the corner of the room, facing the table.  The table top is bare, except for the layers of dust which have collected there.

The house is completely still.  Small swirls of dust appear here and there where drafts disturb them.  Almost completely bare, there are a few pieces of furniture left.  You have a strange sense of disturbed peace in this place.
Would you like to leave?
You almost stumble as your searching reveals a small ring in the floor.  Brushing aside the dust you notice the outline of a trap door in the floor.  Will you open it?
The door opens silently.  A small iron ladder descends to a tunnel ten feet below.  Will you descend?
A small iron ladder leads up.  Will you climb it?
A bedroom.  All that remains in this undisturbed room are a plain four poster bed and the huge head of a blue dragon mounted above the headboard.  Nothing else is of interest here.
This room is totally empty.
A large contingent of Griloch have been making plans here.  They heard your clumsy entrance and are prepared for you.  They attack!
In a well thought out plan, the large contingent engages you and three fighters break for an escape.  You had better destroy the main force quickly.
Only two of you will have the chance to chase them down.  Who will it be?

You discover a piece of paper on one of the bodies.  It reads, "Speak Thyrr at the doorstep?  What does this mean, and who is this Thyrr!?"  It is signed,                Yrrek, Sub Commander NW Region
Around the corner you hear some shouting.  You recognize the word Griloch and know you have stumbled upon a Griloch camp.  They are unaware of your presence.  Would you like to suprise them?
They react quickly as trained soldiers.  You are an even match.
The kitchen.  Cooks and waiters run around each other in what can best be called controlled chaos.  They cook and sweat and cook some more.  One cook shoos you out of the way.
"I hope you are enjoying your stay.  Would you care to check out?"
"That's great.  By the way.... You owe us 10 more gold.  Who will be paying?"
"Well!  No money?  I'll be taking the key then.  Come back when you can afford it."  He takes your key.
"I hope you enjoyed your stay.  Thank you and have a great day."  He takes your key.
You do not have the key to the rooms located upstairs.  From behind you a man behind a counter watches you closely and  loudly clears his throat.
Your key unlocks the door so you can continue through the check point.

A man is alone on his front porch, rocking in a rocking chair.  He sees you and asks if you have seen a beautiful woman wearing a red dress. She has long, flowing, brown hair, and deep dark eyes.  Seeing your blank stares he explains...

"My wife Rina has been missing for three days now.  I've just now returned from an exhausting search, and I fear the worst.  The last I saw of her she was preparing dinner for me and my two boys.  If you see her, will you bring her to me?
"I understand your not wanting to get involved.  Thank you for your time.  Good day to you."  The man continues his rocking.
"Many thanks to you.  Good luck in finding my Rina."  He continues rocking not missing a beat.

The man stops rocking.  He looks up at you and sees his wife Rina. Tears slowly well up in his eyes and run down his cheeks.  Rina runs to him and falls into his arms.  The family is united again.  You explain to the man how you rescued her from the...
The man looks up from his chair and knows you do not have Rina.  He continues rocking not looking at you.
A small family is gathered outside this house, and are just sitting down for a picnic.  Some families can eat at anytime.  They wave to you politely.

The woman of the house stands and walks over to you.  "So, you seek Rina.  Rumor has it she snuck off to meet her lover, Jordag.  I don't beleive it though.  She was a happy woman with a family and a man who loves her deeply.  Hope you find her."
An old man yells at his dog to get out of his bushes.  He nods at you and continues yelling at the dog who has thoroughly destroyed a once beautiful hedge.

An old man runs over to you.  "Rina is a good woman.  She would never betray her husband.  Fine woman.  Real fine looker too.  Purty hair. If I was only twenty-one again.....ahem....anyway, foul work is afoot here.  Hope ya find her."
A huge castle shoots skyward in front of you.  Dark maroon in color, it eerily groans and moans in the wind.  The door is unlocked as no one expected to be found here.  Will you enter?
A great door is here unlocked.  Do you wish to leave the castle?

The walls in this room are lined with swords of all types.  Gleaming bright broadswords, longswords, shortswords, scimitars.  Truely remarkable weapons.  Once you are entirely in the room some of the swords animate and attack!
The swords fall to the floor with a clang; no longer animated.  Would you like to examine them?
The swords are no longer remarkable, having lost their shine and gleam.  They are nothing more than useless pieces of badly dented steel.
A staircase leads up.  Take it?
Stairs leads down.  Take them?
You have intruded upon the lair of some very undesirable creatures.  They protect their home.
You discover some of the things these nasties have collected.
A hulking man of incredible girth greets you.  "My name is Delnoth.  I am the leader of this small community.  Greetings to you.  Will you come inside and dine with me?"

Delnoth leads you inside.  His home is not one of comfort...or cleanliness.  He is not fond of cleaning, as the stacks of dirty dishes would attest.  He feeds you some type of stew....from what, you decide not to ask.  He speaks, "I have been chosen...

...by the people in this community to protect them as my father has and as his father before him.  I have failed.  My people have been ransacked and terrorized by huge worms of purple hue.  They seem to know when to attack.  I....
...am powerless to stop them.  I have failed my people."  He lowers his head and gobbles down some stew waiting for you to say or do something.

"Your words are kind, but they help me not.  I am a failure, that is sure.  But I vow on my girth and strength that I will protect these people, at whatever cost.  Thank you for joining me for dinner.  I must turn in.  Good night."
"I invite you into my home and offer you food and all you do is insult me.  These are not words of a good people.  I must now ask you to leave, for you have insulted my family name."  Will you leave?
"I cannot believe your insolence.  I have no choice."  Delnoth draws his sword and attacks.

The commotion has drawn the attention of the locals.  They yell and shout, "They killed Delnoth!  Get them!  Catch them!  String them up!"  It doesn't look good.  The commotion has also drawn the attention of some of the creatures...
...to which Delnoth was referring.  The huge worms begin munching at random on the people Delnoth swore to protect.  Will you join the fray and help the people or leave them to their fate?
The screams are loud and there is dying everywhere.  You manage to make good your escape and leave the townsfolk to their fate, knowing full well what that fate will be.
After killing Delnoth you decide to help the townsfolk defeat the Purple Worms.  You jump into the fray and try to help the people of this small community.

After the battle one of the men walks up to you carrying the mauled body of his wife.  "I wish I could thank you.  I cannot.  You killed Delnoth and your actions are responsible for these deaths.  But, without your change of heart more...

...would have died.  With that in mind we part; not friends, not enemies, we part."  The man walks away in silence, as do the rest of the few survivors.  You leave the town, knowing you will never be welcome in this community again.
This door is locked up tight.

Delnoth escorts you to the gate.  "I had wished you were of higher character so we may have worked together to fight these worms.  I was wrong.  You will no longer be welcome here."  He closes the gate behind you and locks it.

A small community is nestled here.  Small children scamper around their mothers and fathers, playing various games.  Suddenly a large man appears from one of the huts and blows a whistle three times.  All of the children run to their homes...

...with their mothers and fathers.  Mere seconds later the men return with swords in hand ready to fight an unseen monster.  The large man yells, "Not bad, men.  Twenty-seven seconds.  You'll have to get better than that if you want to save...
...your families.  We will drill again later."  The huge man returns to his home, the children peek out of their houses and finally return to the games.
The lair of the Purple Worms.  You discover some of the items these nasties have collected.

Delnoth looks up from his stew.  "You would do this?  It is settled then.  I will join you as we attempt to root out these Purple beasts and save this community."  Delnoth gathers his things and you begin your search for the worms.

You eat in uneasy quiet as Delnoth just stares and picks at his food.  This goes on for what seems an eternity until Delnoth breaks the silence.  "I am a proud man but not a foolish one.  I thought I alone could protect this town.  I was wrong.  Will...
...you help me in my quest to rid my community of these worms?"
"I understand.  Thank you for dining with me.  I have much training to do if I am to save these people.  I must turn in.  Good night."

Delnoth falls to his knees.  "We did it.  All the weight of the world is off my shoulders.  I cannot tell you how grateful I am.  Let us return to my village and relay the good news."  You return to the village.

You make your triumphant return to the small community.  One by one the townsfolk wander out of their homes as word of your mighty deed spreads like wildfire.  A cheer goes up, "All hail Delnoth, our champion!  All hail our new...

...found friends!"  There is much rejoicing and celebrating for hours and hours.  After most of the rabble rousing has settled down, one of the elder members of the village approaches you.  "I dabble in the healing arts and have become quite good..

...at it.  You may visit me at any time for your healing needs.  I will gladly reduce my fee to you because of your good deeds."  He leaves.  Your work here is done.  You have saved this small village from certain death.  Congratulations.
One of the village elders has set up a small healing facility here.  His prices are outrageous.

The people of the village sense you have not defeated the purple worms as yet.  They also see that Delnoth is not with you.  Some of the women cry, as do the children.  The men bow their heads and say a small prayer.  The people still...
...have high hopes that you can find and defeat the monsters.  They send you on your way.

As you head into the small village, a small boy runs up to you.  Seeing the broad smiles on your faces he realizes you have accomplished your task.  His small face brightens.  He runs to his house and returns with his father.  The news...

...of your victory travels fast.  Soon the  village rushes to the gates to greet you.  They soon realize that Delnoth is not with you.  Some women weep, others pray.  They lament his death, but cheer him as their hero.  They will celebrate his efforts.

There is much rejoicing and celebrating for hours and hours.  After most of the rabble rousing has settled down one of the elder members of the village approaches you.  "I dabble in the healing arts and have become quite good..

...at it.  You may visit me at any time for your healing needs.  I will gladly reduce my fee to you because of your good deeds."  He leaves.  Your work here is done.  You have saved this small village from certain death.  Congratulations.
The village elder offers you his healing services.  His prices are greatly reduced.

Delnoth speaks.  "Thank you again for making me a success as my father was and as his father was before him.  I am always in your debt.  Feel free to come here and visit anytime."  Delnoth looks tired.  He waves you farewell.
The people of the village rush to you.  They wish you good luck and send you back on your way.
The people rush up to you.  They exclaim, "A secret pass!  This must be where the worms sneak into our village.  You must be on the right track."  They send you on your way.
Delnoth is currently not home.
Delnoth informs you all is well.  He thanks you again for your help and assures you he will need no further assistance as he has gotten the community whipped into excellent fighting condition.
Delnoth is busy drilling the community and yelling at the men for taking too long to come to arms.  "You people have got to move faster!"  He looks at you and gives a wink.  He loves his job.
Delnoth chats with you about how the community has come together since the worm incident.  "Never before have these people been so determined to thrive, " he says.  All is well here.
"Thank you for your cooperation.  We must protect our borders.  Please feel free to enter our land via the front gates off of the main road.  Good day to you."  The patrol escorts you to the border.
This rough, rocky terrain provides great hunting ground for the rock spider.  A group of them attack.
The giant snake loves to hunt in this type of country.  A group attacks you.
Some giant boars were out rutting when you interrupted them.  Just your luck, some giant scorpions happen to be in the area.  They join the fray.

A seedy looking furfoot looks up at you.  "So, you got what I need?   You brought me what I asked for?"  He sees you are not whom he expected.  "'scuse me, thought you were someone else.  Welcome to 'Thugs for Hire'. I see by your...
...attire you are not looking for employment, so I ask you, are you in need of one of us?"
"Then I bid you good-day.  Come back anytime."  He closes the door quite hastily.

"Come in then.  Please, have a seat.  We are 'Thugs for Hire'.  We charge a lot; a lot more than that rinky dink outfit to our south.  Bunch-a no good cutpurses they are.  They'll rob ya blind if ya turn your back on them.  But we, we are....

...honest thugs.  We believe you get what you pay for.  And with us you only get the best.  Business has been good so I have only three thugs left for hire that I can show you.  Don't worry, these are good thugs.  We only allow one hire....
...per party at any one time.  The cost is 500gp/week.  I will send one of my associates to find you and collect every week.  Pick one that interests you."  He hands you three sheets of paper.
The furfoot waits patiently as you look over the names.  "So, who looks interesting?"
An excellent choice.  Styx is well known for his staff work.  Rumor has it he has been dabbling in the dark arts as well.  He is 9th level.  Will you take him?
"An excellent choice.  Who will be paying the initial 500 gold?"
"We will be happy to fulfill your request when you have the funds to do so.  Thank you for visiting 'Thugs for Hire'.  Have a great day."  He quickly slams the door behind you.
A man in dark robes appears out of nowhere.  "Sorry to intrude, but you owe us 500 gold.  Who will be paying?"
"Thank you and we will see you in  a week."  As quickly as the robed man appeared, he vanishes.
"No gold, no thug."  As soon as the robed man appeared, he vanishes, along with your hireling.
The furfoot opens the door and coldly states, "You have a balance due of 500 gold.  Who will pay?"

An excellent choice.  Nehpets is one of the most hungry swordsmen I have ever met.  He has one of the biggest appetites I have ever known in a fighter.  He is hungry, very hungry.  He is 11th level.  Will you take him?
"That's fine.  Come back when you are in need of our services.  Thank you and come again."  He shuts the door.

"Thank you for your business.  As long as you keep your credit good we will continue doing business.  When you are done with the hireling bring him/her back here.  Thanks again and we will be in touch with you in a week.  Good bye."
"Welcome back.  Would you like to return your hireling?"
I hope everything worked out for you.  Would you like to hire someone else?
"Sorry to hear about Nehpets.  He ate a lot.  I guess my food bill will be lower anyway."
"Too bad about Holly.  She was a good fighter.  She had many friends.  Many, many friends.  They will all miss her I'm sure.  I know I will miss her."
"Sorry to hear about Styx - he was a good man.  I will miss him."
"Well, thank you for the business.  Come back whenever you need our services."  The furfoot shuts the door.
"A wise choice.  Holly is a formidable opponent with those daggers of hers.  She is very accurate with them.  She is 11th level.  Will you take her?"
The furfoot greets you, "Welcome back.  Here are the names of the people we have for hire."
Nehpets growls, "By the gods I'm starving to death.  Don't you people have any food?  I know a great restaurant way over in Turnstil.  Wanna go?"
Nehpets complains, "All we do is walk, walk, walk.  Do you people ever eat.  I don't mean these rations either.  I know a great restaurant in Turnstil.  Let's go there."  Do you?
Nehpets looks as if he is going to burst.  "I can't take this anymore.  I need to eat.  Eat I say.  I need to eat some food.  There is this great place in Turnstil.  Wanna go eat, huh?"

Nehpets looks grim.  "I don't think I can take this much longer.  I need good food soon.  I need to eat.  Look at my size!  A man of my girth needs nourishment.  I can't live on these rations.  I need to eat real food.  Soon."

"I guess I can stick it out a little longer.  I do need to eat.  I guess if I have to I'll stay with you, but I sure would like to eat soon.  I'm a hungry swordsman y'know."  His words grate on you like a forever dull axe on a sharpening stone.

"As a matter of fact, I'm leaving.  I must have food.  I have to eat.  I'm a very hungry swordsman y'know.  Bye."  He packs up his gear and waddles off to stuff even further his already disfigured torso.
Nehpets burps approval of the decision as he slobbers down the last of his "own" rations.  "Off to dinner!  Follow me."  He leads the party towards Turnstil, and dinner.
Your journey is a long one.  You have travelled many miles and come to the outskirts of a tiny village.  A large group of Trolls are lumbering about and they spot you.  The battle is joined.

You wonder aloud as Nehpets did not survive the battle, "Was his death such a bad thing?"  No one in the party openly disagrees.  With Nehpets dead you can continue on at your leisure.  Maybe someday you will find "his" restaurant.
Victorious in battle, Nehpets absent mindedly wipes his sword as his little mind returns immediately to the task at hand...food.  "Now, off to the restaurant."  He marches off and you accompany him.

"Ahhh, we have arrived."  Nehpets bangs open the door and saunters inside.  "Hallo?  I'm here, bring on the food!"  A waitress cautiously walks over and offers you menus.  You notice these are different than the others in the place.  Nehpets...
...has such an appetite he gets his own menu, and much higher prices!  "This is the best little joint in all of the land.  Lets order!"
The waitress walks over and asks for your order.  "What will you have?"
A modest sign proclaims this the, "Runabout Eatery."  Will you enter?
