You are seated at a lovely table near the bar.  This is a small building, measuring twenty feet square at the most.  Best described as cozy, the Runabout Eatery has more tables per square foot than you could have imagined.  A waitress appears.
She hands you each a menu and asks, "What would you like?"
The door to the restaurant.  Would you like to leave?
Crawling out of the sea are some ugly, ugly water snakes.  You spot them before they spot you.  Would you like to attack them?
A hoard of water snakes have slithered out of the sea in search of prey.  They found you.
At least a dozen slimy creatures have oozed or slithered their way to shore in search of food.  You make an easy target.  They attack.
What would you like to do?

Your waitress points to the south.  "The bar is over there.  The scruffy man with the big belly will help you out."  You can tell by the tone in her voice she does not hold the bartender in  high regard.
This cell is currently unoccupied.

The inhabitant of the cell notices your effort to escape.  He speaks, "Psst.  Come 'ere.  I'll be brief.  Either you let me out and help me escape, or I yell like bloody murder."  Will you let him out?
"Well, I warned ya.  GUARDS!!!!!"  He screams bloody murder and a few seconds later the Turnstil militia is upon you.
A small wooden shack sits here.  It is presently unoccupied.
You fail in your efforts.
The lock springs open and you can enter enter the room.
Some sort of anti-magic shell in the area fizzles your attempt.
The door is answered by a striking young elven woman.  She greets you, "Hello.  My name is Iliyar.  Please come in."  Do you enter?
The house is very tidy.  Rich cherry wood is the theme throughout.  Iliyar asks, "So, you have heard about our difficulties here of late?"

"Let me explain.  We have lost something near and dear to us.  You see, we are in posession of a very powerfull healer.  We can summon him in the tower of Alardeen.   The only problem is, we have forgotten the entry word to open the tower.

"The only one who knows the entry word is our Dwarven friend Dlyven.  He has not been back here in weeks.  That is not unusual as he likes to adventure.  Could you track him down for us and get us our entry word back?"
"I understand.  If you change your mind I'll be around."  She bids you good-day and you leave her home.
"Thank you for your help.  When you discover the word go to the temple and speak it."  With your quest in hand you move on.
Iliyar greets you, "I hope everything is going well!  Good luck!"
Iliyar asks,  "Good.  Will you help us?"
An old temple is locked up tight.  What would you like to do?
Nothing happens.

With a tremendous groan the gates swing open.  Out from the darkness a low light begins to shine.  Growing brighter and brighter, it is almost too much to look at.  A booming voice calls out, "Enter all who needs healing."
Iliyar runs out of the house, "Thank you all so much for reopening our temple.  We do not have much but I can offer you this."  She gives you a bag of Jewels.
An ancient temple.

A young dwarf comes to the door.  "Yes.  What is it?  Not often I get visitors."  He shuffles back and forth on his feet contemplating this uncomfortable silence.  "Oh...ummm...come in, come in."  Do you enter?
A simple home of considerable age is this.  He speaks, "Yeaap, this place is kinda my home away from home.  I love to adventure, ya know.  So, what brings ya here?"
Don't know much about that.  Sorry.
The dwarf looks at you blankly and begins again to contemplate this odd silence.  Anything else you want to know about?
A stoutly woman begs you come her way?   Do you?
"Greetings.  My name is Milna.  Welcome to our village.  You look like big strong men.  I've lost my shoe down the well.  Will you fetch it for me?"
"Oh, thank you.  I'll be here when you bring it back."
The round woman greets you as you approach.  Seeing the shoe in your hand she grabs it lovingly and caresses it.  She turns to you, "Thank you all.  Thank you very much."  She leaves.
The town well.  You notice a small ladder descending into the darkness.  Odd, you don't seem to remember seeing that before.
Will you descend?
The town well.  It is clean, cold water and serves this village well.  You see a set of hand steps descending into the darkness.

You climb and climb.  A small side tunnel intersects the well from the south.  It is man sized and appears to head south for a ways.  You cannot descend further as the water is lapping at your boots.  Will you enter the chute?
Deciding not to go into the chute and retrieve the shoe, you return to the surface.
The hand ladder ascends to the surface.  Go up it?
Ahh.  The shoe is here.  A brown boot-like item reminding you of pain, not comfort.  Do you take it?
As you reach down to grab the shoe, the beast that put it there attacks, seeing easy prey!
Having dispatched the nasties, you retrieve the shoe.
A grand home lying secluded in the woods is locked up tight.  You mill about for a few seconds, then a crossbow bolt lands at your feet and explodes.  No one is injured but you get the hint.
A sign outside this small shop reads "Magicus Plenticus."
You stumble upon a woman who is being threatened by five rather large thugs.  It appears they are robbing her.  Do you intervene?
The largest of the thugs sneers in your direction, "So, it's a fight you be lookin for, eh?  It's a fight you got!"  The battle is joined.
The town guard is quick to show up and help defeat the thugs.
The woman is very grateful.  She hands you a package showing you her gratitude.  You open it and are surprised at its value.
One of the Turnstil guards walks up to you.  "Thank you, good citizens, for aiding one of our own.  Now be on your way for we have work to do cleaning up this mess."
A small house sits peacefully still.
A whisper comes from the house.  "Psst...I'll give you 3000 Gold for that +2 longsword ya got."  Do you accept?
An arm sticks out of the house, and holds out a bag.  You take the bag and hand over the sword.  The deal is done.
Small closed shutters can't hide the bright light eminating from the house.  You swear you hear "Aieeeeeee!!!!" but you aren't completely sure.
A small sign declares, "Stubby's Supplies."  Do you enter?
A one armed man sits atop a barrel in the corner of this well stocked supply shop.  The prices are very reasonable.  "What would you like?"
"Jobs....Hmmm.  Check the job board to your left against the wall."  You turn around and examine the job board.  Anything interesting?
A beautiful gravesight.  It seems the family of this man has taken great care of his final resting spot.  The only thing strange is, you cannot make out the writing on the headstone.
Your searching reveals a trap door located beneath the headstone.  Would you like to descend?
Stairs leads up to a trap door.  Take them?
A huge undisturbed tomb rests here.  The lid is long sealed.  Will you open it?
The lid looks very, very heavy.  Who will try this?
Couldn't budge it.

With all your might you manage to slide open the tomb's lid, revealing its contents:  a human male skeleton, wearing the most gleaming plate mail.  More likely than not a very important person.  Everything is in place except for one peculiar thing.
This man's scabbard is empty.  What would you like to do?
The Sword of Jolak begins humming as you present it in front of the tomb.  The humming grows louder until an almost deafening harmonic echoes in your head.  A blinding flash momentarily stuns you.

You clear your head and look at the tomb.  The scabbard lies across the chest of Jolak, properly housing his sword.  His gleaming armor now resides in your arms, a gift from the long dead man.  You have returned The Sword of Jolak to its owner.
Your attempts reveal two things....a high concentration of magic is in this area and this guy is way too dead to revive or animate.
As you reach into the tomb to steal the armor, a terrifying electricity fills the air.
Electrocuted!
The open tomb reveals King Jolak at peace, his sword in its scabbard across his chest.

This open tomb reveals a human male skeleton, wearing the most gleaming plate mail.  More likely than not a very important person.  Everything is in place except for one peculiar thing.  No Sword. What would you like to do?

A small hut overlooks Lake Hasgen.  A human male is wandering near the shore of the lake and notices you.  He comes over and introduces himself.  "My name is Waldin.  I am the caretaker of Lake Hasgen.  Feel free to enjoy it."
The open door easily opens.
Someone left supplies here.
An empty home.
"Here is all the information we have on this job.  Funny, I don't have any reward listed with this one.  Oh, here it is....You can keep what you find along the way."
The mountain passage leads to an open glade.  Not a creature stirs in the glade.  It is silent.  Too silent.
Peering into the darkness you see nothing at first.  As your eyes begin adjusting to the darkness you can make out two slit like eyes glaring at you out of the cave.

With tremendous speed, a huge, dark shape leaps over you and lands in the glade.  A huge black dragon faces you, its neck weaving to and fro in an almost hypnotic motion.  It speaks to you in common tongue.  "I am Morduun, most....

...ancient of black dragons."  You notice the hilt of a sword sticking out of his back where his tremendous wing is attached.  "Ahhh, you see Jolak's sword," he hisses.  "Causes me great pain, but is a good reminder of the puny man once known....

...as Jolak.  He and I did battle for hours, but I bested him and he lies dead in his tomb.  My wounds are nothing compared to his death.  I read your thoughts.  You seek this sword?  Interesting.  I, of course, will not allow you to have it."
He rears back on his haunches and lets out an ear shattering roar.  The battle for Jolaks sword is waged.
With a tremendous groan Morduun joins King Jolak in death.  You extract the mighty sword from Morduun's still corpse.
In the back of this cave you find Morduun's treasure stash.
"Funny, I don't have any reward listed with this one.  Oh, here it is....You can keep what you find along the way."

A large group of Turnstils finest are assembled here.  Commander Tregel, a dwarf of wide girth, steps forward.  "Men, our mission is to capture and return Jurol Knarl to the Turnstil constable for trial.  Each group will be assigned a sector of....

...land to search.   You must return him alive to the King's courthouse in order to collect your reward of 10,000 gold.  Be warned.  Jurol Knarl is a vile, cunning criminal who would rather slit your throat than be returned to face possible......

...execution.  Take extreme caution in apprehending this evil man."  Tregel starts handing out maps of areas to be searched.  You step forward to receive your assignment.  "Area 51.  Good luck men."  Tregel hands you your map.
The remnants of a well hidden campfire are here.  Only your heightened sense of awareness on the hunt allowed you to notice it.

The ranger notices something hidden near the fire.  A piece of a letter.  It reads, "Your affair with my wife Thantro is over.  I have discovered your plans and have put a stop to them....for good."  That is all you can make out.

You notice some movement in the bushes.  It is Jurol Knarl.  He launches a hail of arrows but you deftly dodge them as they whizz past your heads.  As quickly as you saw him, he disappears into the woods.
Out of nowhere a hail of arrows plunges into the party.  You turn to see where they came from but no-one is visible.  It must be Jurol Knarl.

You cross paths with a group of Turnstil militia also in the hunt.  They explain having seen a fire pit in the area but no sign of Jurol Knarl.  They also have some wounded.  A hail of arrows was the culprit.  Shot from Jurol Knarl's bow!

Your searching allows you to come upon a lucky sight.  Jurol Knarl is hunched behind a tree with his back to you.  A giant boar, lined up in his sights, is about to become dinner.  He does not notice you.  Do you yell for him to give up or attack?
Jurol Knarl stands straight up and turns to you, his back against the tree, the boar making a break for it.  Jurol Knarl speaks, "I am an innocent man.  Hear my story before you take me in."
As you draw your weapons and begin your attack Jurol Knarl yells, "Wait.  Wait.  I am an innocent man!  Hear my story before you attack!"  Do you stop and listen to his story or continue your attack?

Jurol Knarl lowers his bow and speaks, "I did not kill Thantro.  I loved her.  She was to leave Lamsor and spend her life with me away from Turnstil, away from all it stood for.  But Lamsor found out about us.  He is the..

..one who had her killed and framed me as the murderer.  I have proof."  He slowly puts his hand in his pocket.  "A letter.  I have a letter which explains it all."  A panicked expression comes over his face.  "It....it's gone.  The letter.  I ...
...I swear.  It must have fallen out of my pocket.  Please, believe me."

Jurol Knarl has seen you first.  He had a giant boar in his sights, now he has you.  He speaks, "You will listen to my story and you will take me to where I want to go."  It seems you have no choice as the rustling in the trees indicates you are...

Jurol Knarl brightens,  "You do?  Excellent.  You will not regret this decision.  There is a place I can go.  I have a map.  I will be safe there.  Or, I can help you uncover the truth about the murder.  I'll stay with you if you like, or I'll go on my...

Saying your farewells, you bid Jurol Knarl good-bye and good luck.  You have bigger quests to accomplish....destroying Griloch.
The bartender looks you over.  "All the drinks come enough fer all of ya.  Aahh, patrons.  What say yer tastebuds?"

Good, hearty brew.  Not for the faint of heart.  Sticks to you.
An interesting cross between white wine and beer.  Very tasty indeed.
Good grog.  A hint of muskiness underscored by a titilating pinch of sweetness.
As you wipe the drool from your chins, the bartender clears his throat, "Who's payin'?"
"Thanks for your money!  Hope you enjoyed your swill!"
"The Mayor is currently unavailable.  Come back later."
"The Mayor is out to lunch.  You will have to stop back later."
"The Mayor is on a fishing trip at Lake  Miwson.  You will have to try back later."
The castle guardhouse.  It would have been wise to avoid this after you sneak into someones castle.  The guards attack.  But first they sound the alarm!!!

The castle guardhouse.  Seeing you are escorted by their own, they nod and send you on your way.
The lock holds!
Success!!

Not much activity in this well adorned house of justice today.  The guards nod to you and you move on.
With reward in hand and the congratulations of many, you head off in search of more adventure.
Your brave friends have been killed.  The fighters have escaped.  You can only imagine what lies ahead now!

The Griloch fighters have escaped.  You can only imagine what lies ahead now!

"Assault Darken Castle?  It's your choice.  Here is a map.  Kill the overlord of the Castle and collect your reward of 25,000gp."
"King Dranak is powerful indeed.  Remove him from his tyranical reign and receive 500 gems.  We have no information on where he resides or even where his kingdom is."  Good luck.
A traveller from Impossible Quests shows up and gives you your reward.
The Gnoll grumbles.  "Unk.  You no git quest til yu finish quest.  Jizkra Mopuur!"  He shuns you.  You still have a quest pending.
With quest in your heart and absolutely no idea where to start, you head out.
Wandering undead of the castle attack!
You couldn't see the large spear like trap that nearly impaled the leader of your party!!  Though quick to evade death, some injury is still taken.
This dingy room is home to a group of zombies chewing up some human remains.  They spot you and attack.
The human remains held some treasure.
A large creature has been residing in this room.  You have interrupted him.  It attacks.
A pile of human remains is located in the center of the room.  Care to investigate?
Who will investigate?
You have contracted a serious disease.  Your skin starts to itch and burn.  You had better get that checked out or cured in a hurry.
There is nothing of value in the remains.
Dancing swords sing together in an eerie incantation.  Luckily you arrive just as they are finishing up.  A large demon appears amidst the swords and, as a chorus, they attack.
What a nasty critter.  You move on.
This room is currently unoccupied.

This huge chamber is odd indeed.  Shrouded in darkness, the back third seems even darker then the rest.  You think you see some movement against the far wall, but aren't sure.  You sense strong evil here.

Out of the darkness comes the master of the castle.  A demon lich!  Beautiful at first, it growls at you, "Who dares invade my most unholy sanctuary?  You will not only pay with your lives, you will pay with your souls!"

The demon looks over your party and stares at Nehpets.  "Yobtaf, good to see you again."  Nehpets looks back, "Master, I am here to serve you."  The Dark Master magically transforms Yobtaf's weapon.  Yobtaf joins his master in attacking you.
This door is locked up tight.  Unholy magic  pulses from it.
The door pops open.  You may enter.

"I was doomed to be the Dark Master's concubine for all eternity.  I cannot tell you how grateful I am."  She lowers her head and sobs tears of relief.
Congratulations!  You have rescued Rina!  You untie her hands and she joins you.  Now, you must get her home.
The Dark Master's treasure is here as well.
Evil minions patrol the hall.  They attack.
A glowing portal stands here, its energy tingling your every sense.  Step into it?
Your head spins as you sail through time and space.  You end up outside on the castle grounds.

...Dark Master and how he planned to enslave her for eternity.  The man speaks, "You are truly a noble lot.  I do not have much, but I do have some.  Here, take this."  He hands you a bag.  You open it and remove the contents.
You thank the family for this precious gift and head on your way.  Congratulations!  You have returned Rina and completed this quest!
Rina and her husband rock together in their chairs.  All is well.
The Dark Master laughs and spits in your face.  An acidic drool burns your skin.

As you touch the final piece of the spear a low rumbling begins to shake the very ground upon which you stand.  The skies above begin to churn and boil with a pale white-blue light.  The three pieces of the spear suddenly appear a full twenty feet..
..above, hovering within the churning skies of light.  The three pieces meld together becoming one with the light and transform themselves into a wondrous spear which falls to your feet.
Superb!  You have received the Spear of Light.  Now you are getting somewhere.  You can continue on your quest.
Using your oars, you easily control the boat.  Which direction would you like to head?
Without any way to control this thing you keep getting pushed back into the shore.  Looks like you need to find some oars.

You shake the cobwebs out of your head and realize you have been teleported back to shore.

It will be here when you come back.  Unless, of course, someone wants to go fishing.
Your boat rests here safe and sound.  Would you like to use it?
You set sail.  Wind in your face and the smell of sea air refreshes your spirits.
Some large sea creatures attack you from a nearby reef.  You will be able to flop around on the shallow reef, but your movement is severely restricted!
You arrive at your new location and securely anchor your craft.
A large contingent of Cheltin troops is here to greet you.  "Welcome to the Cheltin lands.  Please enjoy your stay here with us."  You exchange pleasantries and move on.
Where would you like to sail?
This door is unlocked.  When you touch it, evil minions of tremendous magnitude pour forth from under your very feet and attack.  This is a nasty surprise.

An empty house.
When you speak the word "Jurol," you think you see a light go on and out in the cabin for just a fleeting moment.

Jurol is here alone.  He shakes his head.  "This is no proof.  Now I must go back into hiding for awhile.  You risk everything by coming here without proof.  You must have in your possession an incriminating letter from Griloch to him!"  Do not...

Brandishing the Spear of Light when you enter this castle proves wise.  As you touch the unlocked door, evil minions of tremendous magnitude pour forth from under your very feet and start to attack.  The spear glows a bright blue.
White flame shoots forth from the tip of the spear and drives the evil horde back into the ground.
A tremendous evil force keeps you outside the gates of this castle.
A small group of kobolds has been roped into evil servitude.  Scared but fiercely loyal they fight with fanatical devotion.
Having vanquished this 'formidable' force, you gather your reward.

"Adventure.  Here's an adventure.  Try being wed to an ungrateful wife for 30 years.  Ya know, I've been trying this new diet but it hasn't been working out.  I'm trying to lose 120 pounds but she just won't leave."  He continues rambling...

...but you try to tune him out.  You fail in your efforts.  He continues, "Adventure is the way of life.  Why just the other day, or was it year?  Anyway,  I was back home and going to the healer when it hit me.  I need an adventure.  So I left.  Just..

...packed up and left.  They probably miss me.  Don't know the word to open the temple I 'magine.  Yep, I'm the only one who knows 'Nylican.'  No one but me.  So, anyway.  I've got adventuring to do, so have a good day."  He sees you out.
"I've heard of it.  I thought it was held by some crazy disappearing dwarf.  Not sure though."

A small shop here is stocked with unbelievable items.  The prices are a little high.
Would you like to leave the Castle?

A gruesome sight indeed greets you.  Four poor adventurers have fought their last battle within these walls.  Nothing remains but rotted corpses, the open mouths frozen awide in fearful screams.  Maggots feed on the...

You efforts prove fruitless.
Your spell reveals a small loose stone in the floor.  Apparently one of the poor saps from down the hall was able to hide this before his demise.  Under the rock is a small, round shiny object.
A tremendous, evil eminating castle looms before you.  Only the Spear of Light keeps you from running away in fear.  Would you like to enter now?

A plethora of undead attack you on sight.

The dark servants have collected a pile of treasure here.

Sliding off the lid reveals nothing but a dusty, old, empty coffin.  You replace the lid and continue adventuring.  Nothing to see there.
All Dead.  No Battle.

...spear.  It has been haunting me for millenia.  You have saved me the trouble of collecting the pieces myself.  I now have the power I need to wreak my vengeance upon the entire land.  You and your pitiful band will go down....

A lever is in the down position.  Would you like to put it in the up position?

Some broken floor tiles mar what is an otherwise flawless design.
A static envelope engulfs your party.  You momentarily lose consciousness.  When you awake you are in some cemetary.
The castle shakes momentarily as a blue hue covers an area on the floor to your north.

As the lever snaps into place, a large gaping hole ringed by fire appears in the floor to the north.

With evidence in hand, together with your testimony, you have proof of Jurol Knarls innocence and you can bring justice to Turnstil.  You head out.
...surrounded.  You get the feeling each arrow is pointed at someone's head.  You hope it's not your own.  Will you listen to his story or attack?
Jurol and his friends unleash a volley of arrows that plunge into your party. Unfortunately some were aimed at your head.

...Allstin and you and Jurol not knowing what to make of this.  Jurol continues, "King Allstin has been in league with Griloch for years; secretly helping him achieve his evil goals.  Guards!  Arrest King Allstin on charges of treason!"

King Allstin sees Jurol with you and  becomes livid.  He screams, "How dare you desecrate this castle by bringing this infidel to my home?  Guards!  Arrest this man and throw him in the dungeon."
Having no physical evidence of the King's possible involvement in all of this, you can say nothing as Jurol Knarl is taken away to prison.

The King turns to you.  "My kingdom is under assault by evil creatures of all sorts and you waste my time by bringing this man to me?  Be gone from my home and do not return here again."  You are roughly issued out.
The south gates of Castle Glisoor.  The guards posted there notice you and shoo you along.

"Good citizens.  Our land is being assaulted by all manner of evil beast.  Now my lovely wife has fallen victim to these vile villians.  I charge you with discovering and defeating this menace before all of our land is overtaken by evil.

Empty barrels line the walls.
Empty, open crates are strewn about this corner.

You are greeted at the door by bouncer Grulk.  "You have an outstanding balance.  With penalties and fees and late charges and gratuities and taxes and surcharges.."  You can see his mind whirling in a cloud of additive mayhem.  He continues, "...that...
...comes to 25 gold.  Will you pay me now or come back when you have it?"  Would you like to pay him now and enter?
Grulk is stunned.  He speaks, "You still don't have it.  Get outta here!"  He kicks you out of the doorway.  The tumble was rough and you are injured slightly.
The lock on the door has not been repaired as of yet.  A lone woman is here changing into her nightgown.  She is very comely.  She is also naked.  She also has a very loud scream.
The lock on the door has not been repaired as of yet.  A lone woman is here combing her hair in front of a mirror.  She is very comely.  She is also half naked.  She also has a very loud scream.
The lock on the door has not been repaired as of yet.  A woman is here washing her face.  She is very attractive.  She is also very naked.  She also has a very loud scream.
The town guard is immediately on the scene.  Wow, they move fast.  After a quick explanation of how you must have the wrong room or something they ask you to leave.  Do you?
The woman flees the room in a total state of hysteria.  As the guards draw their swords they let you know how unfortunate your decision to stay was.  They attack.

The guards escort you back to the hallway and sternly warn you to choose more wisely the rooms which you decide to enter.  As they leave you hear one guard say something under his breath, "Gotta get the owner to fix that lock..."
Slaughtering the Turnstil guard is no way to win their favor.  You step over the bodies and contemplate your decision.  Surely more guards will arrive soon to investigate.

Turnstil guards ride up to you.  The captain speaks, "'Scuse me, but we'd like to ask you about a bloody murder scene we came upon a few days back.  Apparently some thugs broke into a lady's room and after she called for help they murdered the...
...guards.  Do you know anything about this?

"Ah, so you are liars as well as murderers.  You will come with us.  Your description matches perfectly those for whom we are looking."  Out of seemingly nowhere a full 100 armed men cuff you and drag you off.

"I thought you might.  You will come with us peacefully then.  Your description matches perfectly those for whom we are looking."  Out of seemingly nowhere a full 100 armed men cuff you and drag you off.
Court for murder.
A town guard shows up.  "All right.  Your time is up.  You are free to go.  He opens your cell and escorts you out."

The town guard rides up.  About 50 of them.  The Captain speaks, "You were told to go to court.  Now you will come with us and we will escort you there."  They bind you and take you to the courthouse whether you want to go or not.
A staircase leads to a door.  It is locked.
The lock pops open and you make good your escape.

The town guards swarm around you.  Justice Swyfft speaks, "How dumb are you to escape?  The fine is now 155 gems.  Not gold.  Gems.  If you do not have it, you will be put in jail for another 45 days.  Who will pay?"
"Thank you.  Please come again soon."  He closes the door."
"Guess you'll have to come back when you got the money.  Till then we won't be doin' business with ya."  He slams the door.
...destroy Griloch and his mighty army.    Be strong, friends.  Your quest is not an easy one."  The apparition fades.
This secret chamber is lined with odd, pure silver torches, all shining with a magical pale light.  There are plenty for everyone.  Would you like to take them?
In the center of the room is a large brazier, burning with a deep, dark red flame.  Glowing coals pop and sizzle under this perpetual flame.
You easily outrun them, but they still pursue.
The shadow mummies finally reach you and attack.
Weapons drawn, you charge the mummies, screaming your most blood curdling battle cry.
The silvery torches you possessed, fizzle out and fade into nothingness.
Shadowy figures lurch from the shadows and attack as you disturb the unholy fire.

The brazier is cold and black.  No heat or light eminates from it.
Hanging, suspended in air, is a piece of an ordinary looking spear.  You can grab it easily.  Upon closer inspection you realize this is a piece of the Spear of Light!  Congratulations.
Hanging suspended in the air is a piece of an ordinary looking spear.  You can grab it easily.  Will you?
The keeper of this dungeon had one more trick up his sleeve.  Touching the spear opens a small side chamber from which emerge a plethora of greenish mummies.  They attack.

The corridor stops suddenly here in a dead end.
An empty desk occupies this wall of the room.
Some of the shadowy visages you ran from are here waiting for you.  They attack!

A satisfying plate of delicious orange herbed rice and some blue fish.  Most delightful.  The waitress comes over.  "I hope you enjoyed your meal.  Who is paying?"

Chef's splendor should be relabeled as Chef's blunder.  Who knows what you just ate.  The waitress comes over.  "I hope you enjoyed your meal.  Who is paying?"

The waitress thanks you for your stay.  "Please come back anytime.  If you ever see someone named Nehpets Yobtaf let him know he still has a tab here."  She departs as do you.

The town guards swarm around you.  Justice Swyfft speaks, "How dumb are you to escape again?  My judgement will be quick.  Banishment from Turnstil."  He bangs his gavel and the guards escort you to the border and toss you out.
A huge lock has been placed on this door.  Guards peer through the eye slit and seeing it is you close it again.  You really are banished.

Upon seeing you again, Justice Swyfft shakes his head and mumbles something under his breath.  "Okay, that is it!  Anytime I see you, from now on, you will be beaten like dogs and hauled away to the edges of all of Allstin!"  As his name...
...is Justice Swyfft you are quickly taken out back and flogged.
The entire militia escorts you to the edge of the land of Allstin and you are flogged again for good measure.
The captain of the guard turns to you almost begging, "Please, do not come back to Turnstil."  They leave you.
With map in hand you discover a secret door.  Would you like to enter?
A passageway slowly descends and winds deep into the earth.  Bodies are haphazardly tossed here and there along the route.  You emerge in a dark cavern.
A dark passageway leading up is cut through the stone.  Care to take it?
"I'm sorry.  Only one job at a time.  You still have work to do on a previous job.  Try again when you complete what you are working on."

The assistant shuffles through what looks like hundreds of papers.  "Ah, here it is."  Blowing the dust off, she reads, "Ahem... the red dragon menace has been terrorizing the local populace for months now.  Seek and destroy these beasts and...
...receive 3,000 gold.  Here is the information we have on the red dragons."
Up in the sky you hear a terryfying scream.  Looking up you notice three small dots streaking toward you.  As they unleash flame from their jaws you realize you are under attack from Red Dragons!
Having defeated the dragons, you look skyward more often than you think needed.
Cleverly hidden behind some shrubbery is the outline of a huge stone door.  Care to investigate?
Sliding open the huge stone door reveals a passage leading back into the mountains.
A huge stone door stands open.

The tunnel ends and a cave opens into a hot, steamy grove of rocks and debris.  Other caves gape at you from various locations in the mountain walls.  Some rather charred bodies are randomly strewn about the grove.

Your moving about near the caves has brought the attention of the inhabitants.  Out from the cliff walls high above your head a full 12 Red Dragons sweep down and attack.  You have intruded upon their lair.
Congratulations!  You have put an end to the Red Dragon menace.  Their singed carcasses litter the area.
An empty cave.
In the very back of the cave you discover the dragons hoard.
Out of nowhere a man from the mayor's office appears.  "Here is your reward."  He hands you a bag containing the gold.  He then vanishes into thin air.
You are standing in front of the huge stone door.  Would you like to leave?
The town guard notices you are back in Turnstil.  You are taken before Judge Swyfft.
A narrow passage through the rock permits you to sneak in or out of Turnstil.
A lone Berhune cleric has taken up refuge here.  He offers you his services....for a hefty fee.
Stairs lead up to a trap door.  Would you like to open it?
The trap door is so well hidden no one could ever find it without knowing where it is first!
Hidden almost perfectly under a cut piece of sod is a trap door.  Would you like to open it?
Cut stone stairs lead down into a dark dungeon.
A huge stone door stands open.  Care to enter?
A passage cut from the stone itself leads back into the mountains.

The partially charred remains of a dwarf lie here, facing the caves to the west.  A look of terrified horror is forever burned into his face, his back is nearly unharmed.  He is wearing a backpack.  Like to look into it?
Among some personal affects, including a non-functioning compass and some rather inedible food rations, you find a map.

The partially charred remains of a dwarf lie here.  A terrified look of horror is forever burned into his face, which is turned toward the caves to the west, his back is nearly unharmed.  He is wearing an empty backpack.
A pile of sunbleached bones.  Scrape marks on the bones indicate someone--or something--has been feasting on the scraps of flesh.
An illusionary wall!
A lone patrol of four orc guards stand watch here.  With surprise and alarm in their eyes they attack with vigor.
Having heard the commotion, more orcs pour in from somewhere around the corner.

A large table rests in the corner of this room.  Two chairs are neatly pushed under it, one at each end.  On the top rests some papers.  One stands out.  It reads, "Captain, all the structural repairs are completed.  You may inhabit at once."
A large patrol of orcs lead by two minotaurs attack.
A small guard force notices you milling about and attacks.
A large group of minotaurs are drilling some orc guards.  They get your scent and attack.

A large oaken table fills the center of the room.  A full 50 chairs line the sides and ends of the table.  The top of the table is laid out in an exact replica of the city of Turnstil, with troop numbers and strengths written in different areas.
While looking at the table you hear a commotion outside the door to the south.  You can hide under the table and hopefully not be noticed, or wait and fight.  The door is opening.  What will you do?

You cram under the table.  The room fills with orcs, minotaurs and some Griloch higher ups.  They all take their places around the table, waiting for their leader to speak.  Finally, a large human dressed in red robes stands and speaks....

"All hail Griloch!"  The crowd rises and yells in return, "ALL HAIL GRILOCH!"  The gathered group settles back into their seats and the man in red robes addresses them. "The time grows near. Turnstil will soon be under Griloch's control.  Our friends in

the city tell us our plan is working.  Soon we will have all the key players in place so we may carry out our courageous leader's plan.  The table in front of you lays out the battle plan for the invasion of Turnstil.  We will release Turnstil from

the bondage of the Berhune and enlighten them to the ways of Griloch.  As soon as we receive the sign from our allies to the east, we move."  A great cheer erupts.  He continues, "We all have our duties to perform in order to be

in readiness when the sign comes.  That is all."  The crowd erupts again, "ALL HAIL GRILOCH!!"  After a small amout of talk of no great importance the group disperses and you are again alone in the room.

Brave you are, for a full contigent of minotaurs, orcs and Griloch pile into the room.  Spotting you arrogantly standing there in open defiance they waste no time in drawing their weapons and attacking.
Having disposed of this group of Griloch followers, you search the bodies and come up with some paltry booty.

On the body of the red robed mage, you find a speech.  It reads, "The time grows near.  Turnstil will soon be under Griloch's control.  Our friends in the city tell us our plan is working.  Soon we will have all the key players in place so we may carry...

...out our courageous leader's plans.  The table in front of you lays out the battle plan for the invasion of Turnstil.  We will release Turnstil from the bondage of the Berhune and enlighten them to the ways of Griloch.  As soon as we receive the..
sign from our allies to the east, we move.  We all have our duties to perform in order to be in readiness when the sign comes.  That is all.  Dismissed."
A very bloody altar is built here.  On top of the altar lies the body of a Berhune worshipper, adorned in the blue robes of the religion.  His throat slashed and tongue cut out, he is quite dead.

A small guardhouse is littered with dead and dying guards.  One guard struggles to lift his head from the table and musters up a weak voice, "You.  You must help us.  Our icon has been stolen by the Lurha family.  Please return it before we all....
...die.  Please.....help us."  A few more guards stir and lift their heads to see your response.  Will you help them?
"Bring the family back here for justice.  They have killed this once fine community.  They will pay with their lives.  We want  our revenge!   Thank you for your help."
The south gate of Ahcrahn.
"You have condemned us to death.  Please leave us to die in peace."
A small guardhouse is littered with dead and dying guards.  "Please, begin your quest to find the Lurha family...we haven't much time!!!"
More guards appear behind you and, somehow, cut you off.  You are trapped.  They  are not impressed with your cowardice.  They attack.

You lift the icon high above your head.  The constable and the guards stop in their tracks.  They all fall to the ground, sobbing tears of happiness.  You explain how you found the icon and that the Lurha family was unjustly accused of the crime.

The constable looks you over and speaks, "It appears we have done a great wrong to this family.  The Lurha family was noble and well respected before the icon was stolen.  The icon's disappearance thrust this community into chaos and....

...suspicion.  The evidence to frame the Lurha family was strong and we were blind to their honorable standing in the community.  We, all be it wrongful, cast them out.  Now we know the truth which we should have known in our hearts.

The Lurha family was not in any way involved in the theft of our beloved icon and therefore their name is fully restored to honor in this and all other communities.  I will see to that!"  The constable takes the icon from you...
...and you follow him to a dead tree.
The constable places the icon into a hollow in the tree.  In mere moments you are witness to a tremendous transformation.

Dead groves of trees turn green again. Homes previously in disrepair are transformed back to new.  The health of the citizens is returned.  The town is restored to its previous glory.  The Constable turns to you, "Our city is...

...returned to us because of your bravery, courage, and wisdom.  Most of our belongings rotted away when the icon was gone, but one item in particular showed no ill effects.  This has been in our keeping for years, but I know not what...

...it is for."  He reaches into a secret hollow in the tree and pulls out a blue, spear head, the sharp edge shining in the sun.  Presenting it to you he says, "Do with this what you will, and know in your hearts you are always welcome in the...
...city of Ahchran.  You take the gift.
The town guard is not here.  They are working with the citizens of Ahcrahn rebuilding this town.
The townhouse has been cleared out and is now the Lurha family residence.  They are out and about helping to rebuild the city.
He did not realize what he had.  You have gained a piece of the Spear of Light.  Congratulations!
An elegant guard house houses 15-20 guards.  They smile and wave and get back to their duties.
A temple of Berhune.  A cleric greets you.  "How may I ease your suffering?"
The Brunar constable is seated here with two burly guards on either side.  They are currently interrogating a small hill giant who is most displeased.
Griloch has roped some spiders into his web of evil.  They attack.
Griloch's eight legged warriors spot you and attack!
Spiders!  Spiders!  Everywhere spiders!
In the heart of this multi-entrance cavern waits your deadly hosts.  They take advantage of your hindered movement and strike, gaining surprise!
Sticky webs get caught up on everything you own, hindering your movement.
These spiders were charged with guarding something most sacred.  Now, it is yours!
A large rock is shaped into a concealed door.  Care to open it?
It's very, very dark.  The cave leads back into the rock.
A stone door is open here.  To the south a large cavern.  To the north a foreboding passage.
This cave has been long forgotten.  Dust and debris have been gathering here for years.  It seems those who inhabit these parts have yet to discover it.  It is safe to rest here.
This cave was safe until this lone centipede wandered in and attacked.
A mighty battle indeed.  You lick your wounds and continue on.
Strange sounds and growls leap to your ears.  Who knows what foul creatures Griloch has infested this cavern with.  Are you prepared to continue?

With confidence, or is it foolhardiness, you grip your weapon tighter.  Those adept in arcane knowledge keep ready their spell components. You all open your eyes a little wider and press forward into Griloch's domain.
The passage narrows here.  Strange noises leap to your ears.
A group of whip scorpions spot you and attack.
Giant worms burst through the rock walls and attack!
Some of Griloch's unholy creations attack!
Griloch has released a patrol of Trolls to stop you!  They smell blood in the air and attack.
A party of evil maw wandering the caves find you easy prey!
An army of solsux lead by an evil Griloch minion try to put a stop to your advance.
Griloch's Dark Servants serve their master well.
The Dark Servants of Griloch summon help.
Proto-badgers actually live here.  They don't like intruders.
Undead servants of Griloch are thrown into your path.
Ghouls and zombies lead by a Dark Master attempt to thwart your assault.
A pair of Liches escort some giant zombies.  Together they attack with unholy screams.
Three servants of Griloch spot you and attack.
A pair of Red Dragons has taken up shelter here.  Instead of attacking you the larger speaks in surprisingly clear common tongue, "Do you serve Griloch?"  How do you answer?

"Good.  I'm tired of killing these pathetic ghouls, zombies, dark servants and what have you.  Here, take this.  This may help you in defeating these beasts and help us get some rest!"  With a flick of his enormous tail a sword comes clanging...
...to your feet.

The Dragon speaks, "Now be gone with you before I char your bones!"  You take your booty and make a hasty retreat.  As you leave the Dragons rise from their nest and rumble down the cave.  Moments later you hear a roaring thunder...
The Dragon speaks,  "How unfortunate.  I'm tired of killing pathetic ghouls, zombies, dark servants and the likes of  you.  I'd rather get some sleep."  He and his partner attack.
The dragons were sitting atop a sword.  You grab it.
...followed by some ear shattering squeals.  You can only imagine who just got char broiled.

A shadowy apparition appears in front of you.  Decked in full field plate with glimmering shield in one hand Thyrr speaks, "Friends.  Listen well for the evil here makes it difficult to remain long.   You are near your goal.  The portal ...

...to the north will lead you to Griloch's unholy keep.  It is there that you need to destroy him in order to permanently remove him and his unholy army from our lands.  Be prepared!"  The visage begins...

...to fade.  "Remember.....keep your faith in Berhune and use what you have learned.  Find the Spear of Light that was taken from you and with it destroy Griloch forever!  I see my sword is in need of a match.
Here, take my shield so that you have a completed set."  The vision fades and a shimmering shield lays at your feet.
...to fade.  "Remember.....keep your faith in Berhune and use what you have learned.  Find the Spear of Light that was taken from you and with it destroy Griloch forever!"  The vision fades.
An intense unholy evil radiates from this red, glowing door. Are you prepared  to enter?

Evil laughter fills your ears as does the words of Griloch.  "Fools.  So, my unholy army could not prevent you from entering my domain.  I will be forced to stop you myself.  Unholy warriors of Griloch, I command you awaken!  Destroy..

...these non-believers at once!"  You realize, looking at your map, that some strange evil magic is confusing your x/y coordinates.  Before you get your legs under you, an unholy army is upon you to do their masters bidding.
Griloch's voice booms in your head, "Pathetic fools.  That is but a taste of what lies in wait for you!"
Looks like you came in a one way door!  This demonic portal is not functioning.
You fall into the pit.
Marble tiles outline a very deep pit.  Must be more then 60' as you cannot see the bottom.
This wall was a simple illusion.  You see it for what it truly is, a portal.  Will you enter it?
You reappear in a long hallway, just beyond the portal.
The floor is an odd color here.  Step onto it?
You are teleported into a hallway.
Stairs lead up.  Take them?
You land softly at the bottom of this 100' deep pit.
With a thunderous clang you crash to the bottom of this 100' deep pit.  That hurt!
The beasts that inhabit this pit see you as feeding time.  They begin to feast.
The pit opening is above your head.  What would you like to do?
Your efforts fall way short.  You fail.

Wow.  What a tremendous effort.  You grab some rope, jump up inside the pit, then using super-human balance shuffle up the wall and into the room above you.  You lower the rope down and rescue your friends.  Quite the heroic one time effort.
Wow.  That would have been spectacular.  Except when you get to the top, you realize you have no rope to lower down to your party.  You shimmy back down into the pit.  No way you could do that again.
You sail up the pit and back into the room above you.
Your magic allows you to appear back in the room from whence you fell.

News of your outrageous attack on the guards has reached the King.  He sends out his best troops to apprehend you.  A commander yells, "People.  Stay where you are.  It is useless to resist.  You will come with us."  Do you fight or surrender?

The Commander speaks, "A wise choice.  Punishment, in Cheltin, for your crime is banishment.  You are not allowed to ever return here.  If we encounter you in this town again, you will be severely reprimanded."  You are thrown out.
Rumor's abound that you have returned to Cheltin.  The King's men again approach you and attack, not wavering in their voracity.
More men pour onto the battlefield.  The battle is rejoined.
It won't take long for the King to refit his troops and send them after you again.
The guards, knowing full well who you are, shower you with arrows!
You are forced to retreat.
A large force of the King Cheltin's men are ready to greet you as you stand near the boat.  They are not in the best of moods.  They attack you on sight.

After a long and tough search through this castle.....you discover that the king here is bad man in league with Griloch and has stolen the Icon of Ahchran..((BETA TESTERS---This will be much cooler....but you need the Icon to complete the game.)
Stairs lead down here.  Take them?
An illusionary wall reveals a portal behind it.  Enter?
Atop this pedastal rests the Spear of Light.  It is guarded by some most fearsome beasts indeed.  They attack in a frenzy guarding their master's most precious prize.
Having defeated Griloch's horde, you retrieve the Spear of Light.
Your bodies tense as you see before you the most unholy being of all.  Griloch is seated on his Throne of Darkness.  He is flanked on his left and right by Dark Servants.  Seeing you, he...

...laughs in your face.  Haughtily he shouts, "Ignorant fools!  You challenge me without the Spear of Light?  You are most arrogant.  Minions of evil, destroy them."  Griloch vanishes and leaves his minions to dispose of you.
The Dark Masters summon help.
Looks like you need to find the Spear of Light.

...freezes in his tracks.  He attempts to flee but the Spear of Light glows a bright blue and keeps him from escaping.  He bellows, "So, you have found the Spear of Light and now attempt to vanquish me from this land?  I think...

...not.  Now I can dispose of you paltry annoyances once and for all."  It comes down to this.  Armed with the Spear of Light you challenge the Unholy God himself. The battle to save all the peoples of this world is waged.
Griloch laughs at you.  With a wave of his skeletal hand more invisible haunters are summoned to the fray.
Congratulations.  You did it.  With an unholy scream Griloch is vanquished from this land once and for all.  Congratulations!
The father continues,  "You keep the icon and take it back with you to Ahchran.  The town needs it more than we do."

The townsfolk come out in droves to greet you.  That is, those who are still alive.  They fall to the ground, sobbing tears of happiness.  You explain how you found the icon and that the Lurha family was unjustly accused of the crime.
An empty cave.
This must be your lucky day.  A newly hung sign on the door reads, "Straight Ahead Mapmakers."  Must be a new business.  Do you enter?
A tall, elderly elf is busy at a table scribbling on a map.  He puts aside his work and asks which maps you would like to buy.
The elf bids you good-day.
The elf shuffles through some papers and pulls out the map.  Stretching out his thin hand he asks for 500 gold.  Who will pay?
The elf hands you your newly aquired map.
The elf shuffles through some papers and pulls out the map.  Stretching out his thin hand he asks for 100 gold.  Who will pay?
The elf shuffles through some papers and pulls out the map.  Stretching out his thin hand he asks for 1500 gold.  Who will pay?
The elf shakes his head in disappointment.  He says, "Come back when you have the proper funds to afford these luxuries."  He shows you out.
A band of Hill giants being driven by some Griloch Cavalry decide to practice their maneuvers on you.
Some ogres are being trained here by a wizard.  He commands them to attack you.
A group of Hill giants led by a Griloch wizard attack.
A band of patrolling Griloch spot you and attack.
Orcs and minotaur come out of the nearby woods and attack!
You notice a band of creatures in the distance.  They have not seen you yet, so you can avoid them if you like.  Would you like to take them by surprise?

Shuffling through some papers she reads aloud, "The Island Keep of Lonum has been a source of great evil throughout the ages.  Destroy the Keepers of the Isle and recieve 5,000 gold.  Here is more  information.  She hands you a map.

Shuffling through some papers she reads aloud, "The Giants have been a menace to Brunar for months.  Seemingly growing in number, they are constantly pillaging helpless townsfolk.  Eliminate these creatures in their lair and you can keep...
...anything you find in your quest.  Sorry, I have no map for you on this one.  You're on your own.  That is all I have on this job."

What a spectacle!  A group of drunken Hill Giants are in a fist to fist melee with a group of the locals.  Let me tell you, the Hill Giants are getting the upper hand.  Will you help the locals or let them fight on their own?
Unleashing your weapons, you join in the fray!
In a frenzied panic, the village men break and run!
In what can best be described as a massacre, the village men are wiped out.  Still thirsting for blood, the giants turn their attention to you.

Having wiped out the force of giants, the remaining village men and women come out to claim their fallen loved ones.  A small boy walks up to you with tears in his eyes, "Why would you let my father die?"

The remaining men run to their families and embrace their children and wives.  One of the survivors turns to you.  "Thank you for saving us.  They do this all the time.  I wish someone could find where they live and wipe them out."
An empty cave.
A maurading band of Hill Giants is attacking the town.  They spot you and consider you a part of the town.
In one of the Giant's pockets is scrawled a word - "Oorkluen".  He also has a map in his pocket.
Nothing happens.
A large cave entrance is in front of you.  The rumblings of giants is heard in the background.  What would you like to try?
When you speak the word "Oorkluen" a great rumbling comes from the back of the cave.  Peering inside you notice an open stone door has appeared there.
In the back of the cave you see an open stone door.  Would you like to enter?
A strange passage takes you under the very walls themselves and into a passage running east.
A crude stone door is here.  You easily open it.  Would you like to exit the passageway?
A strange passage takes you under the very walls themselves and out of the cave mouth.  As you exit the cave, the great stone door slams behind you and blends perfectly with the surrounding stone.
Hidden under some rocks, a dark passage descends into the earth and heads west.  Would you like to enter?
A large tunnel is carved out of the rock and continues west for some time.  You emerge from the tunnel in the town of Brunar.
A secret door is hidden in the grass.  Care to enter?
A large tunnel is carved out of the rock and continues east for some time.  You emerge from the tunnel in a secluded grove.
From behind the two huts a group of Hill Giants appears and attacks.  This force represents what remains of the village.  If you win this, you will have cleared Brunar of the Giant menace.
Congratulations.  You have saved Brunar from the Giant menace and completed this quest.
A small group of Hill Giants live here.  They sound the alarm and attack!
The other Hill Giants respond to the alarm.
The house is cleared of all living creatures.
A quick recheck of the empty house reveals a hammer.
Nothing but dead bodies litter the house.

Bunched at the end of this long tunnel is a pile of garbage; all that is left of many long dead parties.  Amidst the trash you find some most valuable items.  Now, if you can just get out of here with them.
A crude false wall.  You easily detect it.

I believe the Griloch are growing in power and must be stopped.  Jurol Knarl is obviously in league with these evil doers.  Times are grim, citizens.  It has been rumored for decades that Griloch has returned, and I fear the rumors true.
A patrol of Berhune troops walks proudly by in an impressive march.  They are flanked by Clerics in flowing blue robes.  Would you like to hail them?

A fighter steps forward, "My name is Toutra.  I am the Commander of this rag- tag outfit.  Yes, its true.  Griloch and his minions have returned.  People do not want to believe it's true, but it is.  We have seen it!"  They move on.

An eccentric cleric steps forward, "Good people!  Beware!  Death awaits you all.  Griloch shall destroy all the land if we do not stop him.  Bushes hiding strong magical dungeons.  Invisible beasts of death.  Beeewwaaarreee!"  He leaves.

A fighter steps forward, "Yes, the rumors are true.  Griloch has returned and has gathered quite a formidable force of followers to pursue his evil ends.  With grim faces, the harrowed patrol moves on.

A cleric steps forward, "Good citizens.  Follow Berhune and stray not to the evil Griloch.  Evil is destined to fail as it feeds only on itself after all else in consumed.  Very similar to the Dracstacion swamp boars of Lithgrove."
A fighter steps forward,  "A warning to you.  Do not stray off the roads and established pathways outside of the cities as Griloch grows more powerful daily."  They move on.

A fighter steps forward,  "Please.  Please be careful.  Our troops are weakened as Griloch grows more powerful.  Stay sharp and try to defeat his minions whenever and wherever you are."  He continues on his way.

A cleric steps forward, "Some say Griloch has returned.  I testify this as true.  Beware in your travels as he enlists all manner of evil beast, and daily he grows more powerful."  The cleric moves on.
Congratulations.  You have completed your mission from Impossible Quests.  A man in dark robes appears from nowhere and hands you a bag.  It contains your payment.  He then vanishes.
The patrol aknowledges your hail but pushes on.  The clerics bless you and wish you safe journey as the patrol continues on its way.
In the distance a Griloch patrol searches for victims.  You could get the jump on them if you would like.  Would you like to attack them with surprise?

The evil king's men lay dead along with many a good soldier.  Two armed men return to the grand chamber with the King.  They also have a letter in their hands.  One of the guards speaks, "This man is NOT King Allstin.  His real name...

...is King Dranak!"  He reads from the letter.  "Griloch, my people grow more passive daily as our plan comes to fruition.  Soon no one will suspect me.  As soon as I remove the Jurol problem we can make our move.  I have my best men..

...searching for him and he will be in our grasp shortly.  I await your response.   Yours Eternally,                                             King Dranak, Turnstil Commander."  The guard continues, "I can only imagine what would have befallen us if..

...it weren't for you, Jurol Knarl.  Only you and your new friends were able to bring down this evil man from power.  I find it only fitting that a man as great as you should find his place where it belongs, as new King of Turnstil!"  A huge cheer...

...erupts in the chamber.  "All hail King Knarl.  All hail the house of Knarl.  Three cheers for King Knarl.  Hip, hip, hooray! Hip, hip, hooray! Hip, hip, hooray!"  The crown is ripped from the head of Dranak and placed upon King Knarl's head.  The...

...new King speaks to his people.  "Good citizens of Turnstil.  A great wrong has been righted today.  I have only my new friends to thank."  He looks at you and nods in appreciation.  The crowd warmly applauds you.  King Knarl continues, "But..

...we have a greater evil to destroy.  Griloch and his evil forces still haunt us.  He is the ultimate evil behind all the wrongs that befall us.  I charge all of you as citizens of Turnstil to do your part in ridding the land of Griloch and all...

...his evil forces."  The crowd cheers again.  "Take up arms and fight!  Fight Griloch's evil wherever you encounter it!  I will personally oversee the assemblage of the Turstil army, charged with the utter destruction of Griloch himself.  Join us!"

Another huge cheer erupts as citizens, guards and farmers rush to the King's guards to sign on to this new army.  In the confusion the new King makes his way to you.  "You believed in me.  For that I am eternally grateful.  There are far too few..

...as brave and wise as you are.  Again my thanks.  I guess this is where we say goodbye.  I have an army to build and you are much too valuable to be tied into any civil army.  Go now and continue your quest.  A quest we share together as...

...brothers."  You say your farewells as King Knarl wades into a mass of Turnstil army volunteers.  He turns once more nodding and smiling to you with confidence before he disappears into the masses of his new citizens.
Congratulations!  You have succeeded in your quest to remove King Dranak from power.  A man suddenly appears and hands you a sack.  It contains your payment, plus a bonus.  He vanishes.
With King Dranak removed and King Knarl reigning, Turnstil will become a powerful city once again.  Congratulations.

King Knarl welcomes you.  Flanked by two impressive guards, he speaks, "The army has begun its assembly and grows stronger.  I hope all goes well with your quest.  You may rest here safely whenever you are weary."  He gets back to work.
The gates to Castle Glisoor stand open.  People freely roam around the castle grounds.
